system.description:
Friendly creatures in the area gain +1 to morale and +1 on their “to hit” rolls. The blessing only affects creatures not already engaged in melee. The caster chooses where to centre the spell, at any range up to 6”, and it affects every creature in a 5” square area around that point.

Reverse (curse): enemies in the area suffer -1 to morale and -1 “to hit”.

Components: besides the verbal and somatic components, bless needs holy water; curse needs a sprinkling of specially polluted water.

The cleric speaks a one-word command, in a language the target understands. The target obeys as best it can, but only if the command is absolutely clear and unambiguous. For example, “Suicide!” could be a noun, so the creature would ignore it. “Die!” makes the target fall into a faint or cataleptic state for 1 round, after which it is alive and well. Typical commands: back, halt, flee, run, stop, fall, fly, go, leave, surrender, sleep, rest, etc.

Undead are not affected. A creature with intelligence 13 or more, or with 6 or more hit dice (or experience levels), gets a saving throw versus magic. A creature that meets both conditions does not get 2 saving throws, only one.

The cleric creates four gallons of clean, drinkable water (like rain water) per level of experience: eight gallons at 2nd level, twelve at 3rd, sixteen at 4th, and so on. The water lasts until it is used up, evaporates, is spilled, etc. It can fill any space from the smallest that will actually hold the liquid up to 27 cubic feet (one cubic yard). Water cannot be created inside a living thing.

Reverse (destroy water): obliterates the same quantity of water, leaving no trace (no vapor, mist, fog or steam).

Components: at least a drop of water to create water, or a pinch of dust to destroy it.

By laying a hand on a creature, the cleric heals 1 to 8 hit points of wounds or other injury. The spell does not work on creatures without corporeal bodies, on creatures that are not living, or on creatures that can only be harmed by iron, silver and/or magical weapons. Cured wounds stay healed unless the creature takes further damage.

Reverse (cause light wounds): works the same way and inflicts 1 to 8 hit points of damage. If the target is trying to avoid the touch, the cleric must make a melee “to hit” roll. Caused wounds heal, or can be cured, like any normal injury.

The cleric detects emanations of evil from any creature or object (or of good, with the reverse, detect good). An evil-aligned creature or an evilly cursed object radiates evil; a hidden trap or an unintelligent viper does not. The detection runs in a path 1” wide in the direction the cleric is facing.

Duration: 1 turn + ½ turn (5 rounds, or 5 minutes) per level: 1½ turns at 1st level, 2 turns at 2nd, 2½ at 3rd, etc.

Component: the cleric’s holy (or unholy) symbol, held out in front.

The cleric detects magical radiations in a path 1” wide and up to 3” long in the direction he or she is facing, and can turn up to 60° per round. Stone walls 1’ or more thick, solid metal only 1/12’ thick, or 3’ or more of solid wood will block the spell.

Component: the cleric’s holy (or unholy) symbol.

The spell makes a sphere of light 4” in diameter, as bright as torch light. It lasts for the listed duration (7 turns at 1st level, 8 at 2nd, 9 at 3rd, etc.) or until the caster speaks a word to put it out. The light can be placed anywhere the caster has a line of sight or unobstructed path to, and can spring from air, rock, metal, wood or almost any similar substance.

If cast on a creature, the creature gets its magic resistance and saving throw; if it succeeds, the light appears in the area just behind it instead.

Reverse (darkness): fills the same area under the same conditions, but lasts only one-half as long as the light would.

The spell acts like magical armor on the recipient, forming a barrier one foot away from the body. It blocks bodily contact by enchanted or conjured creatures such as aerial servants, demons, devils, djinn, efreet, elementals, imps, invisible stalkers, night hags, quasits, salamanders, water weirds, wind walkers and xorn. Summoned animals and monsters are kept out in the same way. In addition, attacks by evil creatures suffer -2 “to hit” against the protected creature, and it makes saving throws caused by such attacks at +2.

Reverse (protection from good): works against good creatures instead, but still keeps out enchanted evil creatures.

Components: the cleric traces a 3’ diameter circle on the floor or ground, with holy water (for protection from evil) or blood (for protection from good), or in the air with burning incense (evil) or smoldering dung (good).

Makes spoiled, rotten, poisonous or otherwise contaminated food and/or water pure and fit to eat or drink. Up to 1 cubic foot of food and/or drink is affected.

Reverse: putrefies food and drink, and even spoils holy water. Unholy water is spoiled by the normal (purify) version.

By touch, the cleric gives the recipient courage: +4 on saving throws against magical fear for 1 turn. If the recipient has already failed a saving throw against fear, the touch allows another saving throw with a bonus of +1 per level of the caster (+2 at 2nd level, +3 at 3rd, etc.). Touching an unwilling recipient needs a “to hit” roll.

Reverse (cause fear): the victim flees in panic from the caster at maximum movement speed for 1 round per level of the cleric. Remove fear and cause fear each counter the other.

The recipient’s body is hardened against cold. It can endure zero degrees Fahrenheit without discomfort, even totally nude. Greater cold, such as a sword of cold, ice storm, cold wand or white dragon’s breath, still requires a saving throw, but the recipient saves against cold at +3 and takes only one-half damage on a failed save, or one-quarter damage on a successful one. Lasts 1 turn per level of the caster.

Component: a pinch of sulphur.

Any opponent who wants to strike or otherwise attack the protected cleric must first make a saving throw versus magic. On a failure, it attacks someone else and ignores the cleric entirely. On a success, the cleric can be attacked normally (rolls to hit, saving throws, damage). Area attacks (fireball, ice storm, etc.) are not stopped.

While protected, the cleric cannot take offensive action, but can do anything else that is not an attack, including non-attack spells: healing wounds, bless, augury, chant, casting light in the area (but not on an opponent), and so on.

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol and a small silver mirror.

The cleric asks whether an action in the immediate future (within 3 turns) will help or harm the party. The base chance of a correct answer is 70%, plus 1% per level of the cleric (71% at 1st level, 72% at 2nd, etc.); the referee sets any adjustments for the circumstances. For example, a party thinking of destroying a weird seal that closes a portal could use augury to learn whether weal or woe will be the final result.

Components: a set of gem-inlaid sticks, dragon bones or similar tokens, or the wet leaves left in the cup after an infusion is drunk. If the leaves are used, a crushed pearl worth at least 100 g.p. must be added to the brew before it is drunk.

Once the chant is completed, everyone in the area of effect who is friendly to the cleric gets +1 on attacks, damage and saving throws, and the cleric’s enemies get -1. The effect lasts as long as the cleric stays stationary and keeps chanting. Any interruption breaks the spell, such as a successful attack that causes damage, grappling the chanter, or magical silence.

The cleric can tell whether a person or monster is under the influence of a charm spell. Up to 10 creatures can be checked before the spell ends.

Reverse: shields a single creature from such detection.

All traps in view, magical or mechanical, and whether concealed normally or by magic, become visible to the cleric. The spell is directional: the caster must face a direction to find traps laid in it.

Holds 1-3 humans or humanoid creatures (listed below) frozen in place for 5 or more melee rounds. The duration depends on the cleric’s level: 5 rounds at 1st level, 6 at 2nd, 7 at 3rd, etc.

Saving throws depend on how many targets are chosen: against three, each saves normally; against two, each saves at -1; against one, the save is at -2. A creature that saves is totally unaffected.

Affected creatures: brownies, dryads, dwarves, elves, gnolls, gnomes, goblins, half-elves, halflings, half-orcs, hobgoblins, humans, kobolds, lizard men, nixies, orcs, pixies, sprites and troglodytes.

Component: a small, straight piece of iron.

The cleric reads a person’s aura exactly (human, semi-human or non-human) and learns his or her exact alignment. Up to 10 persons can be examined. Certain magical devices block this spell.

Reverse: completely hides the alignment of one person for 1 turn, or two persons for 5 rounds, etc., even from this spell.

The recipient’s body is toughened to withstand heat, and boiling temperature feels comfortable. It can even stand in very hot or magical fire, such as red-hot charcoal, a large amount of burning oil, flaming swords, fire storms, fire balls, meteor swarms or red dragon’s breath, though these still affect it to some extent: it saves against them at +3, and all damage is reduced by 50%. So it takes one-half damage on a failed save, and only one-quarter on a successful one. Lasts 1 turn per level of the cleric.

Component: a drop of mercury.

Complete silence fills the area of effect. All sound stops: no conversation is possible, no spells can be cast, and no noise of any kind comes out. The spell can be cast into the air or onto an object, and lasts 2 rounds per level of the cleric (2 rounds at 1st level, 4 at 2nd, 6 at 3rd, 8 at 4th, and so on).

It can also be cast on a creature, so that the silence radiates from it and moves with it. An unwilling creature gets a saving throw; if it saves, the effect is centred about one foot behind it instead.

Cast on a poisoned creature, this spell greatly slows the venom. It can even restore to life a victim thought dead, if cast within a number of turns after the poisoning no greater than the cleric’s level: a 10th or higher level cleric can temporarily save a victim poisoned up to 10 turns earlier.

The spell does not neutralize the poison, but stops it doing serious harm while the spell lasts. The victim loses 1 hit point per turn from the venom, but never drops below 1 hit point during the spell. For example, if the victim poisoned 10 turns ago had 10 hit points, the 10th level cleric’s spell leaves him at 1 hit point until the spell ends; hopefully a full cure can be found in that time.

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol and a bud of garlic, crushed and smeared on the victim’s bare feet.

A hypnotic pattern makes one or more snakes stop everything except a slow, semi-erect swaying. The cleric can charm snakes whose total hit points are no more than the cleric’s own; this can be one snake or several. On average, a 1st level cleric could charm snakes totalling 4 or 5 hit points, a 2nd level cleric 9, a 3rd level cleric 13 or 14, etc.

Duration: 3 to 6 turns (d4 + 2) if the snakes are torpid; 1 to 3 turns if they are not torpid but not aroused and angry; 5 to 8 melee rounds (d4 + 4) if they are angry and/or attacking.

system.aoe: One animal within 3” radius of cleric
system.description:
The cleric can understand and talk with any warm or cold-blooded animal that is not mindless (an amoeba, for instance, is mindless). The cleric can ask questions, get answers, and generally be on friendly terms with the animal. Lasts 2 melee rounds per level of the cleric.

Even if the animal’s bent is opposite to the cleric’s (evil/good or good/evil), it and others of its kind with it will not attack while the spell lasts. If the animal is neutral or shares the cleric’s general bent (evil/evil, good/good), it and its companions may do the cleric a favor or service; the referee decides using a special reaction chart, based mainly on the cleric’s charisma and actions.

Unlike speak with monsters (q.v.), this spell only allows conversation with basically normal, non-fantastic creatures such as apes, bears, cats, dogs, elephants and so on.

Calling on his or her deity, the cleric creates a hammer-sized field of force, vaguely shaped like a hammer. While the cleric concentrates on it, it strikes any opponent within range that the cleric chooses. As soon as concentration stops, the hammer is dispelled.

For deciding which creatures it can hit, it counts as a magical weapon of one plus per 3 levels of the caster, but it has no magical bonus “to hit”. Its damage is that of a normal war hammer: 1-6 against man-size or smaller opponents, 1-4 against larger ones. It attacks at the cleric’s own level, just as if the cleric were wielding it.

If the cleric is behind an opponent, the hammer can strike from that position, gaining all the bonuses for such an attack and ignoring defenses such as shield and dexterity.

Component: a normal war hammer, which the cleric hurls toward the opponents while pleading to the deity. The hammer vanishes when the spell is cast.

Turns the bones or bodies of dead humans into the lowest kinds of undead, skeletons or zombies, which obey the caster’s commands. They can follow the cleric, stay in an area and attack any creature (or only a specific type of creature) that enters it, and so on. They stay animated until destroyed or until the magic is dispelled (see dispel magic).

The cleric can animate 1 skeleton or 1 zombie per level of experience: 2 at 2nd level, 3 at 3rd, etc.

Animating the dead is not basically a good act, and clerics of good alignment must use it with careful thought and good reason.

Components: a drop of blood, a piece of human flesh, and a pinch of bone powder or a bone shard.

Like a light spell, except that it lasts until negated (by continual darkness or dispel magic) and is very bright, nearly as bright as full daylight. It can be cast into the air, onto an object, or at a creature. If cast at a creature that makes its saving throw, the light fills the space about one foot behind it instead. Cast successfully on a creature’s visual organs, for example, it blinds the creature.

Reverse: creates a complete absence of light.

The cleric makes food and/or water appear: 1 cubic foot per level of experience. A 2nd level cleric makes 2 cubic feet, a 3rd level 3, a 4th level 4, and so on, in any mix (the 2nd level cleric could make 1 cubic foot of food and 1 of water, etc.). The food is highly nourishing: each cubic foot feeds three human-sized creatures or one horse-sized creature for a full day.

By touching the afflicted creature, the cleric permanently cures most forms of blindness.

Reverse (cause blindness): needs a successful touch on the victim, and is negated if the victim makes a saving throw.

By laying a hand on a diseased creature, the cleric cures most diseases, including parasitic, bacterial and viral ones. The affliction quickly fades, and the creature is whole and well within 1 turn to 1 week, depending on the disease and how far it had advanced.

Reverse (cause disease): the cleric must touch the victim, and the victim must fail a saving throw. The disease takes hold in 1-6 turns. The victim then loses 1 hit point per turn and 1 point of strength per hour, until down to 10% of original hit points and strength, at which point it is weak and virtually helpless.

Neutralizes or negates magic it comes into contact with:

  • It does not affect specially enchanted items: scrolls, magic rings, wands, rods, staves, miscellaneous magic items, magic weapons, shields or armor.
  • It destroys magic potions (treated as 12th level for this spell).
  • It removes spells cast on persons or objects, and counters spells being cast in the area of effect.

Chance of success: 50% base. Add 5% for each level the caster is above the level of the creature whose magic is being dispelled (or above the efficiency level of the object producing it), so a 10 level difference means 100%. Subtract 2% for each level the caster is below. It can be very effective against charmed and similarly beguiled creatures. It always works against the caster’s own magic.

Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the third level magic-user spell feign death (q.v.). The cleric can use it on a character of any level. Components: a pinch of graveyard dirt and the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol.

system.duration: Permanent until discharged Saving Throw: Special
system.aoe: 25 square feet per level of the spell caster
system.description:
A powerful magical inscription that stops unauthorized or hostile creatures from passing, entering or opening. It can guard a small bridge, ward an entrance, or trap a chest or box.

Casting: the cleric traces the sigil (1 segment) and then a web of faintly glowing lines around it, taking 1 segment per square foot protected. The maximum area is 5’ × 5’ per level. When finished, the glyph and lines become invisible.

Effect: any creature that touches the protected area without first speaking the glyph’s name suffers the magic stored in it. Saving throws apply, either reducing the effect by one-half or negating it depending on the glyph. Typical glyphs shock for 2 points of electrical damage per level of the caster, explode for the same amount of fire damage, paralyze, blind, or even drain a life energy level (if the cleric is high enough level to cast that glyph).

Components: incense to trace the glyph; if the area exceeds 50 square feet, it must also be sprinkled with powdered diamond worth at least 2,000 g.p.

Helps find a known or familiar object. The cleric slowly turns and knows when he or she faces the direction of the object, if it is within range: 7” at 1st level, 8” at 2nd, 9” at 3rd, etc. It can find things such as clothing, jewelry, furniture, tools, weapons, or even a ladder or stairway.

Reverse (obscure object): hides an object from being found by spell, crystal ball or similar means.

Neither version affects a living creature. Component: a piece of lodestone.

Gives exactly the same bonuses as a chant: +1 on attacks and saving throws for friends and -1 on the same rolls for enemies. Unlike a chant, once the prayer is spoken the cleric is free to do other things.

Component: a silver holy symbol, prayer beads or a similar device.

Usually removes a curse, whether on an object, on a person, or in the form of an unwanted sending or evil presence. It does not remove the curse from a cursed shield, weapon or suit of armor, for example, but it typically lets the afflicted person get rid of such an item.

Reverse (bestow curse): not permanent; it lasts 1 turn per level of the cleric. The target must be touched, and still gets a saving throw that negates the curse. The usual effects are:

  • 50% of the time: one ability score (chosen at random by the DM) drops to 3.
  • 25% of the time: -4 on the victim’s “to hit” and saving throw rolls.
  • 25% of the time: each turn the victim is 50% likely to drop whatever it holds (creatures that do not use tools simply do nothing).

A cleric can devise his or her own curse, of similar power to these, with the referee’s approval.

The cleric can ask a dead creature several questions within a set time and receive answers based on what the creature knew. The cleric must be able to speak the language the creature used in life. How long the creature has been dead matters, since only higher level clerics can talk with the long dead. The number of questions and the time allowed for asking them also depend on the cleric’s level (see the table).

Components: a holy symbol and burning incense, used on the body, the remains, or part of them.

A stronger form of cure light wounds (q.v.). By laying a hand on a creature, the cleric heals 3 to 17 (2d8 + 1) hit points of wounds or other injury. It only works on the creatures that cure light wounds can affect.

Reverse (cause serious wounds): works like cause light wounds: the victim must be touched first, and a successful touch inflicts 3 to 17 hit points of damage.

The recipient can immediately tell whether the truth is being spoken. Lasts one round per level of the cleric. Component: gold dust.

Reverse (undetectable lie): makes bald-faced lies seem reasonable, or simply counters detect lie. Component: brass dust.

Like augury, but used to learn about an area: a small wood, a large building, a section of a dungeon level, etc. The location must be known. The spell tells the relative strength of the creatures there; whether there is a rich, moderate or poor treasure; and the relative chance of angering evil or good supernatural, super powerful beings if the area is invaded and attacked.

Chance of a correct divination: 60% plus 1% per level of the cleric (65% at 5th level, 66% at 6th, etc.), adjusted by the Dungeon Master for the facts of the area. An incorrect result gives inaccurate information.

Components: a sacrificial creature, incense and the cleric’s holy symbol. An unusually potent divination may require the sacrifice of particularly valuable gems or jewelry and/or magic items.

Ends the possession of a creature or object by any outside or supernatural force. This includes control of a creature by a force in an object, possession by magic jar (q.v.), demonic possession, curses, and even charm, since exorcise works like a dispel magic. It also affects a magic item that is the object of the exorcism: a soul object of any kind that is successfully exorcised makes the life force of the creature concerned wholly and completely inhabit its nearest material body. (Cf. 1e Fantasy RPG, MM, Demon.)

Once begun, the exorcism cannot be interrupted, or it is spoiled and useless.

Chance of success: the base chance is a random 1% to 100% (the referee may instead set it to suit the circumstances). Each turn of the exorcism, roll percentile dice; a roll equal to or less than the chance succeeds. If the cleric’s level is lower than the level of the possessor or possessing magic, subtract 1% per level of difference; if higher, add +1% per level (cumulative). A religious artifact or relic adds 1% to 50% depending on its power.

Components: the cleric’s holy object and holy water (an unholy object and unholy water for evil clerics).

Water or a similar fluid in the area of effect sinks away. It is lowered by 5% of its original depth per level of the cleric: 40% at 8th level, 45% at 9th, 50% at 10th, etc. The area also grows with level (8” × 8” at 8th level, 9” × 9” at 9th, and so on), and the effect lasts 1 turn per level.

Reverse: the fluid rises to its normal highest level plus one foot per level of the cleric.

Components: the cleric’s religious symbol and a pinch of dust.

system.aoe: Creature touched or 1 cubic foot of substance/2 levels
system.description:
The cleric detoxifies any venom in the creature or substance touched. Touching an unwilling opponent, such as a poisonous reptile or snake (or an opponent’s envenomed weapon), needs a hit in melee. The cure is permanent only for poison already present at the moment of the touch; creatures or objects that make new poison are not permanently detoxified.

Reverse (poison): also needs a successful “to hit” touch. The victim gets a saving throw versus poison, and dies if it fails.

Identical in every way to protection from evil (q.v.), except that the globe covers a much larger area and lasts longer.

Components: the cleric traces a circle 20’ in diameter, using holy water or blood, or incense or smouldering dung, as for protection from evil.

The cleric can talk, in very basic terms, with all kinds of living plants. For example, the cleric can ask plants whether creatures have passed through them, make thickets part for easy passage, have vines entangle pursuers, and the like. All plants in the area of effect are under the spell’s command, but it cannot make rooted plants walk. Lasts 1 melee round per level of the cleric.

Components: a drop of water, a pinch of dung and a flame.

Turns 1 stick into a snake per level of the cleric (a 9th level cleric turns 9 sticks into 9 snakes). The snakes attack as the cleric commands. There must be sticks or similar pieces of wood (torches, spears, etc.) in the area of effect; only those are changed. Enchanted items such as magic staves and spears are not affected.

Each snake has a 5% chance per level of the caster of being venomous: 55% at 11th level, 60% at 12th, etc. The effect lasts 2 melee rounds per level.

Reverse: turns snakes into sticks for the same duration, or negates a sticks to snakes spell. The number affected depends on the countering cleric’s level: a 10th level cleric can turn only 10 snakes back into sticks.

Components: a small piece of bark and several snake scales.

The cleric can speak the language of any creature inside the spell area, whether a racial tongue or an alignment language.

Reverse: cancels a tongues spell, or confuses verbal communication of any kind within the area of effect.

Removes the burden of unwilling or unknown misdeeds from the subject, and also removes the effects of a magical alignment change. The subject must be truly repentant, or else not in control of his or her own will and so unable to repent. The referee judges this, taking into account any past uses of the spell on that person. Deliberate, knowing and willful misdeeds cannot be atoned for with this spell.

Components: the cleric’s religious symbol, prayer beads or wheel or book, and burning incense.

The cleric contacts his or her deity, or the deity’s agents, and asks questions that can be answered with a simple “yes” or “no”: one question per level of the cleric. The answers are correct. The referee will probably limit commune to one use per adventure, per week or even per month, since the “gods” dislike frequent interruptions.

Components: the cleric’s religious symbol, holy/unholy water and incense.

A very strong form of cure light wounds (q.v.). By laying a hand on a creature, the cleric heals 6 to 27 (3d8 + 3) hit points of damage from wounds or other injury. It cannot affect the creatures excluded under cure light wounds.

Reverse (cause critical wounds): works like the other cause wounds spells: a successful touch inflicts 6-27 hit points of damage. Caused wounds heal like any other wounds.

Sends evil summoned creatures, or monsters enchanted and made to do evil, back to their own plane or place. Examples: aerial servants, demons, devils, djinn, efreet, elementals and invisible stalkers. The spell lasts 1 melee round per level of the caster, and while it lasts every creature it could affect suffers -7 on its “to hit” rolls when attacking the caster.

Reverse (dispel good): works against summoned or enchanted creatures of good alignment, or those sent to aid the cause of good.

Components: the cleric’s religious object and holy/unholy water.

A column of fire roars down on the exact spot the caster chooses. Every creature in the area of effect must make a saving throw: on a failure it takes 6-48 (6d8) hit points of damage, on a success 3-24 (3d8).

Component: a pinch of sulphur.

Restores life to a dwarf, gnome, half-elf, halfling or human who has been dead no longer than 1 day per level of the cleric (a 9th level cleric can raise someone dead up to 9 days).

  • The body must be whole; missing parts stay missing.
  • The person must make a special saving throw to survive the ordeal (see CHARACTER ABILITIES, Constitution).
  • A raised person is weak and helpless and needs one full day of bed rest for each day spent dead.

Newly made undead (but not skeletons) still within the days-dead limit are affected: they become resurrected dead if their constitution lets them survive, and otherwise are simply dead.

Somatic component: a pointed finger.

Reverse (slay living): the victim gets a saving throw; if it succeeds, the victim only takes the damage of a cause serious wounds spell, 3-17 hit points. An evil cleric can use the reverse freely. A good cleric must be extremely careful with it, being absolutely certain that the victim is evil and that the death is greatly necessary and for good; otherwise the cleric’s alignment will change sharply.

rolls.label: Reverse (slay living): damage if the save is made

system.description:
Everything within the area of effect appears as it really is. Secret doors become plain. Displaced things are seen in their exact location. Invisible, astral and ethereal things become clearly visible. Illusions and apparitions are seen through. Polymorphed, changed or magicked things are apparent. Even creatures’ auras become visible, so the cleric can tell whether they are good, evil or in between.

Component: an eye ointment made of very rare mushroom powder, saffron and fat.

Reverse (false seeing): the subject sees things as they are not: rich as poor, rough as smooth, beautiful as ugly. Its ointment is made of oil, poppy dust and pink orchid essence.

For either version, the ointment must be aged for 1-6 months.

Summons an invisible aerial servant (see 1e Fantasy RPG, MM) to do the cleric’s bidding. It does not fight, but it will find and bring back any object or creature described to it, as long as the servant can physically carry it to the cleric or the cleric’s chosen agent. The caster should keep in mind what happens if the servant is prevented, for any reason, from finishing its task.

Duration: up to 1 day per level of the cleric. The servant returns to its own plane when the spell lapses, its task is done, it is dispelled, the cleric releases it, or the cleric is slain.

Control: when summoning it, the cleric must have a protection from evil spell or be inside a magic circle, thaumaturgic triangle or pentagram, unless he or she has a religious symbol, artifact or relic to control it with. Otherwise the servant kills its summoner and returns to where it came from.

Attacking: on a mission, the servant always attacks with complete surprise and gets 4 free melee rounds. If the target can detect invisible objects, roll a six-sided die instead: 1 = 1 free round, 2 = 2, 3 = 3, 4 = 4, and 5 or 6 = 0 (the target is not surprised at all). Each round the servant rolls to hit; a hit means it has grabbed the object or creature it was sent for.

Grabbing a creature: compare the servant’s strength with the creature’s. If the creature has no strength rating, roll the correct number and type of hit dice for both the servant and the creature; the higher total is the stronger.

A thick cloud of creeping, hopping and flying insects swarms around a point the caster chooses, up to 36” away. The cloud does not move once formed. It lasts 1 turn per level of the cleric, after which the insects disperse.

  • Vision inside is limited to 3”.
  • Creatures inside take 1 hit point of damage per melee round from bites and stings, regardless of armor class.
  • All creatures with fewer than five hit dice check morale. Creatures with two or fewer hit dice automatically flee at top speed in a straight line, in a random direction, until at least 24” from the cloud; those with fewer than five hit dice that fail the morale check do the same.

Countering it: heavy smoke drives the insects out of the smoke’s area. Fire also drives them away: a ring-shaped wall of fire keeps the plague outside it, while a fire ball only clears the insects from its blast area for 1 turn. Lightning and cold/ice work the same way. A dispel magic cast on the summoning point ends the spell. A cube of force (a special magic item) would keep the insects off a character heading for the center of the swarm, but invisibility gives no protection.

Components: a few grains of sugar, some kernels of grain and a smear of fat.

The cleric moves himself or herself, or another creature, to another plane of existence. The subject stays there until sent away by some similar means. If several persons join hands in a circle, up to seven can be shifted at once. An unwilling target must be touched, and also gets a saving throw that negates the spell.

Component: a small forked metal rod. Its exact size and metal decide which plane the subjects go to; the referee determines how, and which, planes are reached.

The cleric compels the target to perform a service and return with proof that it was done. Examples: finding and bringing back an important or valuable object, rescuing a notable person, releasing a creature, capturing a stronghold, slaying a person, delivering an item, and so forth.

If the target does not properly follow the quest (by ignoring it, delaying, or twisting it), it suffers -1 on its saving throws for each day of such behavior. The penalty stays until the quest is properly completed or the cleric cancels it. Some circumstances temporarily suspend a quest and others complete or cancel it; the Dungeon Master gives this information as needed.

Component: the cleric’s religious symbol.

Gives inanimate objects movement and a semblance of life. They attack whoever or whatever the cleric first names. The object can be of any material: wood, metal, stone, fabric, leather, ceramic, glass, etc. The cleric can animate 1 cubic foot of material per level: a 14th level cleric could animate objects totalling no more than 14 cubic feet, such as a large statue, two rugs, three chairs or a dozen average crocks.

Movement depends on how the object moves and how heavy it is. A large wooden table is heavy, but its legs make it fast; a rug can only slither; a jar rolls. Examples: large stone pedestal 1” per round (rocking), stone statue 4”, wooden statue 8”, light ivory stool 12”. Slithering is about 1” to 2” per round, rolling 3” to 6”.

Damage depends on form and material:

  • Light, supple objects can only obscure vision, block movement, bind, trip, smother, etc.
  • Light, hard objects can fall on or strike a target for 1-2 hit points, or obstruct and trip like supple ones.
  • Hard, medium weight objects crush or strike for 2-8; larger and heavier ones for 3-12, 4-16 or even 5-20.

Attack frequency depends on how the object moves, its appendages and how it attacks, from once every five melee rounds to once per round.

Armor class depends mainly on the material and how easy the object is to hit given its movement. Damage to the object depends on the weapon and the material: sharp cutting weapons work well on fabric, leather, wood and the like; heavy smashing and crushing weapons on wood, stone and metal. The referee decides all of these factors, including how much damage the object can take before it is destroyed.

Creates a wall of razor-sharp blades whirling endlessly around a fixed point. Any creature trying to pass through it takes 8-64 (8d8) hit points of damage. The barrier lasts 3 melee rounds per level of the cleric, and can cover any area from 5’ square up to 2” square (20’ × 20’ underground, 60’ × 60’ outdoors).

Summons one or more mammals to the cleric’s location to attack the cleric’s opponents, which they always do. They stay 2 melee rounds per level of the cleric, or until slain.

The total hit dice of the animals cannot exceed the cleric’s level. A 12th level cleric could conjure one 12 hit dice mammal, two of 6 hit dice, three of 4, 4 of 3, six of 2, or 12 of 1. Each +1 (hit point) added to a creature’s hit dice counts as 1/4 hit die, so a creature of 4 + 3 hit dice counts as 4 3/4.

The cleric learns the shortest, most direct route to the destination sought, whether the way to, from or out of a place, outdoors or underground, a trap, or even a maze spell. The cleric knows the right direction that will eventually lead out, and the exact path to follow (or actions to take), for as long as the spell lasts: 1 turn per level of the cleric. It frees the cleric and those with him or her from a maze spell in a single melee round, and keeps doing so for the duration.

Component: a set of divination counters of the kind the cleric prefers: bones, ivory counters, sticks, carved runes or whatever.

Reverse (lose the path): the creature touched is completely lost and cannot find its way for the duration, though it can still be led.

Wipes away disease and injury in the recipient. It completely cures all diseases and/or blindness and heals all damage from wounds or injury except 1 to 4 (d4) hit points. It also dispels a feeblemind spell. Later wounds, injuries and diseases affect the recipient normally.

Reverse (harm): with a successful touch, infects the victim with a disease and inflicts damage equal to all its hit points except 1 to 4 (d4).

For creatures that heal (or harm) cannot affect, see cure light wounds.

The cleric makes water or a similar liquid move apart, forming a trough. Per level of the cleric, the trough is 3’ deep by 1’ wide by 2” long (20’ or 20 yards): at 12th level it is 36’ deep by 12’ wide by 24” (240’ or 240 yards) long. It lasts for the duration or until the caster chooses to end it (cf. dispel magic).

Component: the cleric’s religious symbol.

The cleric can talk with any type of creature that has any form of communication; the monster understands the intent of what the cleric says. The referee checks the creatures’ reaction. All creatures of the chosen type within range can understand. The spell lasts 1 melee round per level of the cleric, and the monsters converse as far as they are able and willing.

The stones in the area speak to the caster, telling who or what has touched them and what is covered, hidden or simply behind them. They give complete descriptions as needed.

Components: a drop of mercury and a bit of clay.

When the word is spoken, the cleric is instantly and infallibly safely transported to his or her sanctuary. The sanctuary must be named in advance and be a well known place, but it can be any distance away, above or below ground.

Besides himself or herself, the cleric can carry 250 gold pieces weight per level (cumulative). A 15th level cleric could carry 3,750 gold pieces weight (375 pounds) extra, which can be equipment, treasure, or living matter such as another person.

The cleric projects his or her astral body into the Astral Plane, leaving the physical body and material possessions behind on the Prime Material Plane (the plane on which the whole universe and all its parallels exist). Only certain magic items that exist on several planes can be taken along.

Travel: the Astral Plane touches the first levels of all the Outer Planes, so the cleric can travel astrally to any of them at will, then leave the Astral Plane by forming a body on the chosen plane. The cleric can also travel astrally anywhere on the Prime Material Plane, but cannot form a second body there. Travel can be slow or fast as the cleric wishes, and the final destination depends on how the cleric pictures it.

The silver cord: the astral body is always connected to the material body by a silvery cord. If the cord breaks, the person dies, astrally and materially, but normally only the psychic wind can break it. When a second body is formed on another plane, the cord stays invisibly attached to it; on return, the cord simply goes back to the material body resting on the Prime Material Plane and revives it from suspended animation.

Limits: as a general rule, an astrally projected person can only be seen by creatures on the Astral Plane. Astral travelers can act on the Astral Plane, but their actions do not affect creatures not existing there.

Duration: until the cleric ends it, or until it is ended from outside (dispel magic, or destruction of the cleric’s body on the Prime Material Plane).

Companions: up to five other creatures linked in a circle with the cleric can go along. They depend on the cleric and can be stranded.

(See APPENDIX IV, THE KNOWN PLANES OF EXISTENCE, for more on the Astral Plane and astral projection.)

Changes the weather where the cleric is when the spell is cast, for 4 to 48 hours (4d12) over an area of 4 to 16 square miles (4d4). Casting takes 1 turn, and the change is felt after another 1 to 4 (d4) turns. It cannot change the temperature radically (from below zero to a 100 degree heat wave, for instance).

All three aspects (clouds/precipitation, temperature and wind) can be controlled, but only to the conditions listed for the prevailing weather:

For example, a clear, warm day with light wind could become hazy, hot and calm. Contradictory combinations, such as fog with strong wind, are not possible. Several control weather spells can only be used one after another. The spell only works where the climate allows the conditions.

Components: the cleric’s religious symbol, incense, and prayer beads or a similar prayer object.

rolls.label: Delay before the weather is felt (turns)

system.description:
A strong local tremor rips the ground, over in one melee round. It affects all terrain, vegetation, structures and creatures in the area, a circle whose diameter is ½” per level of the cleric (a 20th level cleric’s earthquake is 10” across).

Terrain

MarshWater drains off, leaving muddy, rough ground

Components: a pinch of dirt, a piece of rock and a lump of clay.

rolls.label: Creature falls into a crack (killed on a 1)

system.description:
Raises the recipient’s life energy by one level, undoing an earlier level drain by some force or monster. For example, if a 10th level character drained to 9th by a wight receives restoration, he or she returns to exactly the experience points needed for 10th level, with the extra hit dice (or hit points) and level abilities restored accordingly. It only works if cast within 1 day per level of the caster after the level was lost. It also restores the intelligence of a creature affected by feeblemind (q.v.).

Reverse (energy drain): by touch, drains one life energy level (cf. “undead” such as spectre, wight, vampire).

Restores life and full strength to a person dead up to 10 years per level of the cleric (cumulative); a 19th level cleric can resurrect the bones of someone dead up to 190 years. See raise dead for which persons can be brought back.

After casting it, the cleric cannot cast spells or fight until he or she has had one day of bed rest per level of the person restored (or destroyed).

Reverse (destruction): with a touch, in combat or otherwise, the victim instantly dies and turns to dust.

Components: the cleric’s religious symbol and holy/unholy water.

The cleric draws a symbol in the air or on any surface. It glows for 1 turn per level of the cleric. The cleric chooses one of these symbols when casting:

  • Hopelessness: creatures who see it must turn back in dejection and/or surrender to capture or attack unless they save versus magic. Lasts 3 to 12 turns.
  • Pain: creatures affected suffer wracking pains: -4 “to hit” and -2 dexterity. Lasts 2-20 turns.
  • Persuasion: creatures who see it take on the cleric’s alignment and become friendly to the cleric for 1 to 20 turns unless they save versus magic.

Components: mercury and phosphorus (cf. the eighth level magic-user symbol spell).

The spell does two things: it opens an ultra-dimensional connection between the cleric’s plane and the plane of a specific being of great power, so that the being can simply step through the gate to the cleric; and it draws that being’s attention.

The cleric must name the demon, devil, demi-god, god or similar being wanted. Something will certainly (100%) come through. What it does depends on many things, including the cleric’s alignment, the nature of his or her companions, and who or what opposes or threatens the cleric; the Dungeon Master handles this. The being either goes back at once (very unlikely) or stays to act.

The word has tremendous power. It drives evil (good) creatures from other planes back to their own planes of existence. It also affects other creatures of different alignment within the 6” diameter area of effect centred on the cleric, according to their hit dice or level:

Hit dice or levelGeneralMoveAttack diceSpells
less than 4kills---
4 to 7+paralyzes 1-4 turns---
8 to 11+stuns 2-8 rounds-50%-4-
12 or moredeafens 1-4 rounds-25%-250% chance of failure

Severed body parts (fingers, toes, hands, feet, arms, legs, tails, or even the heads of multi-headed creatures), bones or organs grow back. This takes 1 round if the severed part is present and touching the creature, otherwise 2-8 turns.

Reverse (wither): the part or organ touched shrivels and stops working in 1 round, and drops off as dust in 2-8 turns. As usual, the creature must be touched to be harmed.

Components: a prayer device and holy/unholy water.

The cleric’s body, and possibly those of one or two others, turns to cloud-like vapor. A magical wind carries them along at any speed the caster chooses from 6” to 60” per turn. The spell lasts as long as the cleric wishes, up to 6 turns (one hour) per level.

For every 8 levels of the cleric, up to 24, he or she can touch another person and take that person (or those two persons) along. Wind walkers are not invisible, but look misty and transparent; if fully dressed in white they are 80% likely to be mistaken for clouds, fog, vapors, etc.

Components: fire and holy/unholy water.

The druid shows an animal (of at least animal intelligence, but no higher than semi-intelligent) that he or she wishes to be its friend. Only neutral animals can be attracted, befriended and trained. If the animal fails its saving throw versus magic when the spell begins, it stands quietly while the druid finishes casting, and afterwards follows the druid around.

Training: the druid can teach it 3 specific “tricks” or tasks per point of intelligence it has. These are simple tasks, like those taught to a dog or similar pet. Each trick takes 1 week of training, and all training must be done within 3 months of gaining the animal. During training the animal will not harm the druid, but if left alone for more than 3 days it goes back to its natural state and behaves accordingly.

Limit: the druid can attract up to 2 hit dice of animals per level, and can never have more hit dice of such animals than twice his or her level.

Components: mistletoe and a piece of food the animal likes.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the first level cleric spell of the same name.

The druid detects snares and pits along a path 1” wide by 4” long, and so can avoid such deadfalls. Underground, only simple pits are detected, not every kind of trap. Outdoors, the spell detects all kinds of traps: deadfalls, missile trips, snares, etc. Lasts 4 melee rounds per level: 4 rounds at 1st level, 8 at 2nd, 12 (1 turn plus 2 rounds) at 3rd, etc.

Plants in the area of effect (grasses, weeds, bushes, even trees) wrap, twist and twine around creatures there, holding them fast for the duration. A creature that makes its saving throw is not held, but its movement is slowed by 50% for the duration.

Outlines objects or creatures with a pale glowing light, blue, green or violet as the druid chooses. The druid can outline about 12’ of outline per level (one 6’ man or two 3’ kobolds). With enough power, several objects or creatures can be outlined, but each must be fully outlined before the next is started, and all must be in the area of effect.

Outlined objects or creatures (even invisible ones) can be seen 8” away in the dark, or 4” if the viewer is near a bright light. Opponents gain +2 “to hit” against outlined creatures. The light itself does no harm.

The recipient becomes completely undetectable to normal animals with intelligence under 6. Normal animals include giant-sized kinds, but not any with magical abilities or powers. The recipient can walk among or through animals as if not there; he or she could stand in front of the hungriest lion or a tyrannosaurus rex and not be bothered or even noticed. A nightmare, hell hound or winter wolf, however, would certainly notice.

Component: holly rubbed over the recipient.

The druid learns the direction and distance of the chosen kind of animal within the area of effect. Any kind of animal can be sought, but the druid must concentrate on that kind. The caster faces a direction, thinks of the animal, and knows if any are within range. Each round the druid can face only one direction, so only a 2” wide path is known. The path is 2” long per level, and the spell lasts 1 round per level.

The recipient can move through any terrain (mud, snow, dust, etc.) without leaving footprints or scent, so tracking him or her is impossible. The ground passed over does radiate a dweomer for 6-36 turns afterwards.

Components: a leaf of mistletoe (burned afterwards, with the ashes powdered and scattered) and a sprig of pine or evergreen.

The druid gains 100% accurate knowledge of the weather (sky, temperature, precipitation) in a nine square mile area centred on him or her, two hours ahead per level: two hours at 1st level, 4 hours at second level, etc.

Makes dirty, contaminated water clean, pure and drinkable: up to one cubic foot per level of the druid.

Reverse (contaminate water): works the same way, and can even spoil holy/unholy water.

The druid’s own oaken cudgel becomes a magical weapon, +1 to hit, doing 2-8 hit points of damage to opponents up to man-sized and 2-5 to larger ones. The druid must wield it.

Components: an oaken club, any mistletoe and a shamrock leaf.

system.aoe: One animal type in 4” radius of druid
system.description: Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the second level cleric spell of the same name.

The creature’s skin becomes as tough as bark: its armor class improves by 1 place, and it gains +1 on saving throws against all attack forms except magic. The druid can cast it on himself or herself or on any creature touched.

Components: mistletoe and a handful of oak bark.

Affects one person or mammal. Unless it makes its saving throw (which negates the spell), the creature sees the druid as a trusted friend and ally to be listened to and protected. The druid cannot control it like a puppet, but it takes everything the druid says or does in the best light. It would not obey a suicidal command, but might believe the druid who says the only way to save the druid’s life is to hold back an onrushing red dragon for “just a round or two”. The spell gives no extra language ability.

Who it affects: all mammals and all persons. “Person” means any bipedal human or humanoid of about man-size or smaller, including those affected by hold person (q.v.).

Breaking the charm: the creature gets a new saving throw periodically, more often the more intelligent it is; a success breaks the charm. The charm also breaks automatically if the druid harms or tries to harm the creature by some overt act, or if dispel magic (q.v.) is successfully cast on it.

The druid creates pure, drinkable water: 1 cubic foot per level, at a distance of up to 1” from the druid.
The same as the first level cleric spell cure light wounds, except that the druid must have mistletoe (of any kind) to cast it.

Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the third level magic-user spell feign death (q.v.). Components: a piece of dead oak leaf (as well as mistletoe, of course).

The same as the fourth level magic-user spell fire trap (q.v.), except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics and the material components: holly berries and a stick of charcoal to trace the outline of the closure.

Makes ferrous metal (iron, iron alloys, steel) hot. The druid can affect the metal of one man-sized creature (its arms and armor) per level, or a single mass of metal weighing 500 gold pieces per level (cumulative).

The heat builds and fades over the spell’s rounds: the first and last rounds the metal is very warm and uncomfortable to touch; the second and sixth (next to last) rounds it is hot, causing blisters and damage; the third, fourth and fifth rounds it is searing hot, causing damage and disability to exposed flesh:

Metal temperatureDamage per round of exposureDisability
very warmnonenone
hot1-4 hit pointsnone
searing2-8 hit pointshands or feet: 2-8 days; head: 1-4 turns unconsciousness; body: 1-4 days

Wood, leather or flammable cloth touching searing metal smoulders and burns, and then does searing damage to exposed flesh the next round. Fire resistance (potion or ring) or a protection from fire spell completely negates heat metal, as does plunging into water or snow, or a cold or ice storm spell (qq.v.).

Reverse (chill metal): counters heat metal, or else chills metal as follows:

Metal temperatureDamage per round of exposureDisability
coldnonenone
icy1-2 hit pointsnone
freezing1-4 hit pointsamputation of fingers, toes, nose or ears

Chill metal is countered by resist cold or by any great heat, such as being near a blazing fire (not a mere torch), a magical flaming sword, a wall of fire, etc.

The druid can find any chosen type of plant within the area of effect. Only one type can be sought, and the druid must concentrate on it. The area of effect is centred on the druid and moves with him or her.

A misty vapor rises around the druid and stays in that place for 4 rounds per level. It cuts visibility of every kind (including infravision) to 2’ to 8’ (2d4). The cloud is a cube that grows with level: 1” at 1st level, 2” at 2nd, 3” at 3rd, and so on. Underground it is at most 1” high, though its length and width are not limited. A strong wind cuts the duration by 75%.

A flame as bright as a torch springs from the druid’s palm and lasts 2 melee rounds per level. It does not harm the druid, but it is hot and sets fire to flammable materials (paper, cloth, dry wood, oil, etc.).

The druid can throw it as a missile, range 4”. On impact it flashes, igniting combustibles within a 3’ diameter of where it hits, and then goes out. The druid can put the flame out at any time, but not any fires it has started.

Cast on a length of vine, a stick, pole, rope or similar object. The object rises slightly off the ground and trips creatures crossing it unless they save versus magic. It can only trip as many creatures as are actually stepping over it; a 3’ long rope could trip only 1 man-sized creature. Very large creatures, such as elephants, are not affected at all.

A creature tripped while moving very fast (running) takes 1-6 (d6) hit points of damage and is stunned for 2-5 (d4 + 1) rounds if it falls on a very hard surface; on turf or other soft ground it is only stunned for 2-5 segments.

The object keeps tripping everyone who crosses it, including the caster, for the whole duration. Creatures aware of it and what it can do get +4 on their saving throws. It is 80% undetectable without magical detection.

rolls.label: Damage when running on a hard surface

system.description: Bends and warps wood, permanently ruining its straightness, form and strength. Range is 1” per level. Per level of the druid, it affects about a fifteen inch length of wood up to one inch in diameter: at 1st level a druid might warp a hand axe handle or four crossbow bolts; at 5th level, the shaft of a typical magic spear. Boards or planks can also be warped, springing a door or making a boat or ship leak.

There must be a storm of some kind in the area: a rain shower, clouds and wind, hot and cloudy weather, or even a tornado. The druid can then call down lightning bolts, one every 10 melee rounds (1 turn), for a number of turns equal to his or her level (1 bolt per turn per level). The spell is normally usable outdoors only.

Each bolt strikes straight down at any distance the caster chooses, up to 36”. It does 2d8 plus 1d8 per level of the druid (a 4th level druid’s bolt does 6d8). Any creature within 1” of the bolt’s path or the point where it strikes takes full damage, or half the dice on a successful saving throw: against an eight dice bolt, 8d8, or 4d8 if the save is made.
The same as the 3rd level cleric spell cure disease (q.v.), except that the druid must have mistletoe to cast it. It is also reversible to cause disease.

Holds one to four animals rigid for 2 melee rounds per level of the druid. It affects normal or giant-sized mammals, birds and reptiles (apes, bears, crocodiles, dogs, eagles, foxes, giant beavers and similar animals), but not monsters such as centaurs, gorgons, harpies, naga, etc.

Weight limit: 400 pounds of body weight per animal per level of the druid (100 pounds for non-mammals). An 8th level druid can hold up to four 3,200 pound mammals, or four 800 pound non-mammals such as birds or reptiles.

Saving throws: the druid chooses how many animals to target; the more there are, the better each one’s chance to resist. Against 1 animal, it saves at -4; against 2, each saves at -2; against 3, each at -1; against 4, each saves normally.
The same as the 4th level cleric spell neutralize poison (q.v.).

Normal vegetation grows, twines and tangles into a thicket or jungle. Briars, bushes, creepers, lianas, roots, saplings, thistles, thorn, trees, vines and weeds become so thick they form a barrier. Creatures must hack or force their way through at a movement rate of 1”, or 2” for creatures larger than man-sized (the PHB text does not give the time unit). There must be brush and trees in the area for the spell to work.

The area is 2” × 2” per level, in any square or rectangular shape the druid chooses when casting: an 8th level druid can affect up to a 16” × 16” square, a 32” × 8” rectangle, a 64” × 4” rectangle, a 128” × 2” rectangle, etc. The growth stays until cleared by labor, fire, or magic such as dispel magic (q.v.).

The effect depends on who receives it.

On the druid: complete immunity to normal fires (torches, bonfires, oil fires and the like) and to magical fires such as demon fire, burning hands, fiery dragon breath, fire ball, fire seeds, fire storm, flame strike, hell hound breath, meteor swarm, pyrohydra breath, etc. The protection absorbs up to 12 hit points of potential damage per level of the druid and then ends; otherwise it lasts 1 turn per level.

On another creature: immunity to normal fire, +4 on saving throws against fire attacks, and 50% less damage from magical fires.

Needs a fire of some kind within range, which goes out immediately when the spell is used. The druid chooses one of two effects:

  • Fireworks: a flashing, fiery burst of glowing colored aerial fireworks, 10 times the volume of the fire source. It lasts 1 segment per level of the druid and temporarily blinds creatures in the area, under it, or within 12” of it (in every case only those with an unobstructed line of sight).
  • Smoke: a thick, writhing stream of smoke rises from the fire and forms a choking cloud, 100 times the volume of the fire source, roughly globe-shaped from the ground or floor up (or filling the shape of a confined area). It totally blocks vision beyond 2’ and lasts 1 round per level.

system.aoe: 2’ diameter circle plus 1/6’ per level of the spell caster
system.description:
Turns a supple vine, thong or rope into a snare that blends into its surroundings and is 90% undetectable without magic. One end is tied in a loop that tightens around one or more limbs of any creature that steps inside it (the head of a worm or snake can also be caught).

  • If a strong, supple tree is nearby, the snare is tied to it. When triggered, the tree bends and springs back, doing 1-6 hit points of damage and lifting the creature off the ground by the trapped limb(s), or strangling it if the head/neck was caught.
  • With no such tree or sapling, the cord tightens on the limb(s) and then wraps the whole creature, binding it tightly without damage.

Breaking free: for the first hour only storm giant or greater strength (23) can break it. After that it weakens by 1 point per hour (22 after 2 hours, 21 after 3, 20 after 4) until 6 full hours have passed, when 18 strength will break it. After 12 hours the magic is gone and the loop opens, freeing anything held.

Components: a snake skin and a piece of sinew from a strong animal, woven into the cord, plus mistletoe.

system.aoe: Three cubic feet, plus one cubic foot per level
system.description: Exactly the same as the fifth level magic-user spell stone shape (q.v.), except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics and the need for mistletoe as an extra component.

Calls a cloud of flying insects (70% of the time: bees, biting flies, hornets or wasps) or otherwise a swarm of crawling ones (biting ants or pinching beetles). They appear after the spell is cast and attack any creature the druid points to. The victim takes 2 hit points of damage per melee round and can do nothing but try to fend off the insects while they attack it.

The insects can be sent against another opponent, but there is at least a 1 round delay while they leave the first target, and crawling insects move only about 12’ per round (top speed over smooth ground). Underground, the druid might summon 1-4 giant ants instead, but only with a 30% chance unless giant ants are nearby.

Components: mistletoe, a flower petal and a bit of mud or wet clay.

The druid takes the form of a small living tree or shrub, or a large dead tree trunk with only a few limbs. Even the closest inspection cannot tell it is a druid, and for all normal tests it is a tree or shrub, yet the druid sees everything happening around as if in human form. Clothing and gear change along with the druid. The druid can end the spell at any time, changing instantly back to human form and able to act normally.

Components: mistletoe and a twig from a tree.

The recipient can breathe freely underwater for 6 turns per level of the druid.

Reverse (air breathing): a water breathing creature can survive comfortably in air for the same time.

Calls up to eight animals, of no more than four hit dice each, of the kind the druid names, if any such animals are within range. They help the druid in whatever ways they can, staying until a fight is over, a specific mission is done, the druid is safe, the druid sends them away, etc.

The druid can try three times, naming three different kinds of animals: for example, first wild dogs (none come), then hawks (none come), then wild horses, which may or may not be within range. If it is not known whether a kind of animal is present, the referee decides the chances. Apart from giant animals, no fantastic animals or monsters can be summoned (no chimerae, dragons, gorgons, manticores, etc.).

Summons certain woodland creatures to the druid. It works only outdoors, though not necessarily only in woods. The druid must keep casting without interruption until some creature appears or 2 turns have passed (the words and gestures are easy, so this is not especially tiring). Only one of these kinds can be called, and only if some are within range:

2-8 brownies1-4 satyrs
1-4 centaurs1-6 sprites
1-4 dryads1 treant
1-8 pixies1 unicorn

The referee checks the outdoor map, or judges the chance of such creatures being in range from the nature of the area.

Called creatures get a saving throw versus magic at -4 to resist the summons. Those that come are friendly to the caster and give whatever help they can. But if the caller or anyone in the caller’s party is evil, the creatures get another saving throw versus magic, this time at +4, when they come within 1” of the druid or of an evil character with him or her; if it succeeds they immediately try to escape. In any case, if the druid asks them to fight on his or her behalf, they must make a loyalty reaction roll based on the druid’s charisma and any past dealings with them.

Components: a pinecone and 8 holly berries.

The druid can raise or lower the surrounding temperature by up to 9 degrees Fahrenheit per level: a 10th level druid could change it by anywhere from 1 to 90 degrees, up or down. The spell lasts 4 turns plus 1 turn per level (14 turns for a 10th level druid).
The same as the 4th level cleric spell cure serious wounds (q.v.), except that it needs mistletoe of any kind.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the 3rd level cleric spell dispel magic (q.v.).

Creates an illusory forest that looks perfectly natural and cannot be told apart from a real one. Other druids, and creatures such as centaurs, dryads, green dragons, nymphs, satyrs and treants, recognize it for what it is. Everyone else believes it is real, and their movement and order of march are affected accordingly. It lasts until dispelled by the reverse of this spell or by dispel magic.

The forest is generally rectangular or square, at least 4” deep, and placed wherever the druid wants, with its nearest edge up to 8” from the druid. It can be smaller than the maximum area if the druid wishes.

Affects plants in three ways: 1) moving plants stop moving; 2) plants cannot twine, grasp, close or grow; 3) plants cannot make any sound or movement not caused by wind. It works on all vegetation, including parasitic and fungoid types and those magically animated or empowered, such as green slime, molds of any sort, shambling mounds, shriekers, treants, etc. Lasts 1 melee round per level of the druid.

Targets and saving throws: it affects 1 to 4 plants, or 4 to 16 square yards of low growth such as grass or mold. Against one plant (or 4 square yards), the save is at -4; two plants (or 8 square yards), -2; three plants (or 12 square yards), -1; the maximum of 4 plants (or 16 square yards), normal.

Opens a magical passage through trees, undergrowth, thickets or similar growth, even magical growth. Only the caster, higher level druids and dryads can use it. The path is up to 4’ wide, 8’ high, and 12’ long per level of the druid. The spell lasts 1 turn per level.

The druid can also step into a solid tree trunk and hide there until the spell ends. Inside an oak, the spell lasts 9 times longer; inside an ash, 3 times as long. If the tree is cut down or burned, the druid must get out before it falls or is consumed, or die with it.

Creates an ordinary fire up to 12’ on a side. It lasts only a single round, but does 1-4 hit points of damage to creatures in the area and sets fire to combustibles such as cloth, oil, paper, parchment, wood and the like, which then keep burning.

Reverse (quench fire): puts out any normal fire (coals, oil, tallow, wax, wood, etc.) in the area of effect.
Exactly the same as the 3rd level spell protection from fire (q.v.), but against electrical/lightning attacks.

Creates an invisible barrier against insects. Normal insects will not come within 10’ of the druid while the spell lasts. Giant insects with 2 or more hit dice can pass if they make a saving throw versus magic, but even then they take 1-6 hit points of damage crossing the barrier. Only true insects are affected, not arachnids, myriapods and similar creatures.

Components: mistletoe and one of the following: several crushed marigold flowers, a whole crushed leek, 7 crushed stinging nettle leaves, or a small lump of resin from a camphor tree.

rolls.label: Damage to giant insects that push through

system.description: The same as the 4th level cleric spell speak with plants, except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics and the usual druidic material component (mistletoe, et al.).

system.aoe: Up to 8 animals in a 2” square area
system.description:
Up to 8 animals within a 2” square area grow to twice their normal size. Their hit dice double (improving their attacks accordingly) and their combat damage doubles. Lasts 2 melee rounds per level of the druid. It works particularly well with charm person or animal or speak with animals.

Reverse: shrinks animals to one half size, halving hit dice, attack damage, etc. in the same way.
The same duration and effect as the 4th level spell animal summoning I, except that it calls up to six animals of no more than eight hit dice each, or 12 animals of no more than four hit dice each.

Creates an invisible barrier that keeps out all creatures and missiles made of living plant material. The druid, and any creatures inside the shell, are protected from attacking plants and plant creatures such as shambling mounds or treants. Lasts one turn per level of the druid.

The druid becomes one with nature in the area and learns about the surrounding territory: one fact per level. Examples: the ground ahead, left or right; the plants ahead, left or right; the minerals; the streams and bodies of water; the people living there; etc. It works only outdoors, in a radius of one half mile per level of the druid.

The druid can raise or lower the wind force in the area of effect by 3 miles per hour per level. Once cast, the wind changes by 3 miles per hour each round until the chosen speed is reached, and dies down at the same rate when the spell ends. The spell lasts 1 turn per level. Around the druid there is a calm “eye” of 4” radius.

Wind speedIn the airAt sea
over 30 mphdrives small flying creatures (eagle-sized and under) from the skies; severely hinders missile firesailing is difficult
over 45 mphdrives even man-sized flying creatures from the skiesminor ship damage
over 60 mphdrives all flying creatures from the skies; uproots small trees, knocks down wooden structures, tears off roofs, etc.ships endangered
over 75 mphhurricane force: devastates everything but the strongest stone buildingsships sink

A higher level druid can use control winds to counter the same spell cast by a lower level druid (cf. control weather).

Underground: the spell works, but the “eye” shrinks as much as the space confines the wind. If the area of effect is a 48” radius and the space only allows a 46” radius, the eye is 2” in radius; in any space under 44” radius there is no eye, and the caster is caught in the wind too.
The same as the 5th level cleric spell insect plague (q.v.), except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics and the material component: mistletoe, or the holly or oak leaves substitute.

The druid steps into a tree and passes from inside it into another tree of the same type, roughly in the direction wanted and within the range below:

Range of
Type of TreeArea of Effect
Oak60”
Ash54”
Yew48”
Elm42”
Linden36”
deciduous30”
coniferous24”
other18”

Both trees must be of the same type, living, and at least as thick as the druid. If no suitable tree lies in the chosen direction, the druid goes to one that is in range: a druid who enters an ash wanting to go as far north as possible (54”), when the only suitable ash in range is to the south, comes out of the ash to the south.

The passage takes only one segment (6 seconds). The druid can step out at once, or stay in the receiving tree for up to 1 round per level. If there is no suitable tree in range, the druid stays in the first tree and must step out within the same number of rounds. (See plant door for what happens if such a tree is chopped or burned.)

Creates a blazing curtain of shimmering magical fire, yellow-green or amber when cast by a druid. Only the side facing away from the caster does damage:

  • A creature passing through takes 4 to 16 hit points, plus 1 per level of the caster.
  • Creatures within 1” take 2-8 hit points; within 2”, 1-4 hit points.
  • Creatures especially vulnerable to fire may take more, and undead always take twice normal damage.

The wall is opaque. It lasts as long as the druid concentrates on it, or 1 round per level if the druid does not concentrate. It is either a stationary sheet up to 2” square per level, or a ring around the druid, up to ½” radius per level and 2” high, which moves with the druid.

The same duration and effect as the 4th level spell animal summoning I, except that it calls up to 4 animals of no more than 16 hit dice each, or eight of no more than 8 hit dice, or 16 of no more than 4 hit dice each.

Creates a hemispherical force field that keeps out all normal (non-magical) animal matter. A giant would be kept out, but undead could pass through, as could monsters such as aerial servants, demons, devils, etc. Lasts 1 turn per level of the druid.

Opens a special gate to the Elemental Plane of Fire and summons a strong fire elemental (see 1e Fantasy RPG, MM) near the caster. Roll for what comes:

  • 85%: a 16 die fire elemental
  • 9%: 2 to 4 salamanders (q.v.)
  • 4%: an efreeti (q.v.)
  • 2%: a huge fire elemental of 21 to 24 hit dice (d4 + 20)

Because of druids’ bond with natural and elemental forces, the creature will not turn on its summoner, so the druid needs neither to concentrate on it nor to have a magic circle. It helps the druid however it can, including attacking the druid’s opponents. It stays up to 1 turn per level of the druid, or until sent back by attack, dispel magic, or the reverse of this spell (dismiss fire elemental). Only a druid can dismiss summoned salamanders, efreeti or ultra-powerful elementals.
The same as the 4th level cleric spell sticks to snakes (q.v.), except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics and the usual druidic material component.

Turns natural rock of any kind into an equal volume of mud, never deeper than one-half its length and/or breadth. Rock affected collapses into mud. Creatures that cannot levitate, fly or otherwise free themselves sink and suffocate, except lightweight creatures that could normally cross such ground.

The mud stays until dispel magic or the reverse spell, mud to rock, restores it to stone (though not necessarily to its old shape). Evaporation turns it into normal dirt in 1 to 6 days per cubic 1”, depending on sun, wind and drainage.

Reverse (mud to rock): hardens normal mud into soft stone (sandstone or similar), permanently unless changed by magic.
The same as the 5th level cleric spell cure critical wounds (q.v.), except that it needs mistletoe of any kind.

Used only against creatures that cast magic spells: the victim’s mind becomes that of a moronic child until heal, restoration or wish removes the effect. The victim’s saving throw is adjusted by the kind of spells it uses (usually making it harder to save):

Spells used by targetSaving throw adjustment
Cleric+1
Druid-1
Magic-user (human)-4
Illusionist-5
Combination or non-human-2

The spell has no material component.

The druid enters any large plant and, in a single round, travels any distance to a plant of the same species. Both plants must be alive. The destination plant need not be familiar: the druid can simply choose a direction and distance and arrives as near as possible to that place.

There is a 20% chance, less 1% per level of the druid, that the druid instead arrives at a related species of plant 1 to 100 miles from the intended one. If a particular destination plant is chosen but it is not alive, the spell fails and the druid must leave the entry plant within 24 hours. Harm to a plant holding a druid can affect the druid (cf. plant door).

Waves of force roll out in the direction the druid faces, pushing all wooden objects in the path away from the druid to the edge of the area of effect, at 4” per melee round.

  • Firmly fixed wooden objects over three inches in diameter are not affected; loose ones (movable mantlets, siege towers, etc.) are pushed back.
  • Fixed objects under 3 inches in diameter splinter and break, and the pieces are swept along.
  • Wooden shields, spears, wooden weapon shafts and hafts, arrows and bolts are pushed back, dragging their holders with them; a spear planted to resist will splinter.

The path is 12” wide and 2” long per level, and the waves keep sweeping it for 4 rounds per level: a 14th level druid’s spell covers 12” × 28” and lasts 56 rounds (5.6 turns). (This assumes the druid uses greater mistletoe.) Once cast, the path is fixed, and the druid can do other things or leave without affecting the spell.

Creates a barrier of very tough, flexible green tangled brush covered in needle-sharp thorns as long as a finger. Its nearest edge appears up to 8” from the druid, as desired. It lasts 1 turn per level and covers ten cubic inches per level of the caster in any shape the caster wants: a 14th level druid could make a wall 7” long by 2” high (or deep) by 1” deep (or high), a wall 1” high by 1” wide by 14” long to block a dungeon passage, or any other shape that suits.

Damage: any creature breaking through the wall, or merely running into it, takes 8 hit points of damage plus its armor class (so up to 10 more); a negative armor class is subtracted from the base 8. This damage applies for each 1” of thickness. Creatures inside the area when the spell is cast count as having run into it, and must also break through to get room to move.

Getting through: chopping a path through 1” of wall takes at least 4 turns. Normal fire does not harm it. Magical fire burns it away in 2 turns, acting as a wall of fire while it burns (see wall of fire).

Creates fiery missiles or timed incendiaries that burn with great heat. They lose their power 1 turn per level of the druid after they are made (a 13th level druid’s seeds last up to 13 turns). No mistletoe or other material is needed beyond the acorns or holly berries.

  • Acorns (up to four): thrown up to 4”, the target must be struck. Each bursts on impact, doing 2 to 16 hit points (2d8) of damage and igniting combustibles within 1” diameter of where it hits.
  • Holly berries (up to eight): too light to throw well, they are placed, or tossed up to 6’, and burst into flame on the druid’s command word (command range 4”). Each does 1 to 8 hit points (d8) of damage to every creature in a ½” diameter burst and ignites combustibles there.

Creatures in a burst area take one-half damage if they make a saving throw, but a creature hit directly by an acorn always takes full damage.

Similar to the cleric spell control weather (q.v.). The druid calls up weather suited to the local climate and the season. In spring: a tornado, thunderstorm, cold, sleet storm or hot weather. In summer: torrential rain, heat wave, hail storm, etc. In autumn: hot or cold weather, fog, sleet, etc. In winter: great cold, blizzard or thaw. Near coasts, hurricane-force winds can be called in late winter or early spring.

The druid does not control the weather once it comes. It may last a single turn (a tornado) or hours or even days, and cover anywhere from about 1 square mile to 100 or more. Several druids can work together to strongly affect weather, controlling winds and/or summoning very extreme conditions.

Within 4 turns of casting, the coming trend is apparent (clearing skies, gusts of warm or hot air, a chill breeze, overcast skies, etc.), and the weather arrives 6 to 17 turns (d12 + 5) after casting. Using anything less than greater mistletoe sharply limits the extremes achieved.

Makes a separate stone object move (not a piece of a huge boulder or the like); see the sixth level cleric spell animate object. The druid can animate 2 cubic feet of stone per level (24 cubic feet at 12th level), and it stays animated for 1 melee round per level.

The rock attacks, breaks things, blocks, etc. as the druid wishes while the magic lasts. It has no mind or will of its own, but follows its instructions exactly as spoken. It can be given only one set of instructions for one single action, simply worded and very brief (about 12 words).

In a clap of thunder and a cloud of smoke, a large flaming chariot appears, drawn by two fiery horses. It moves 24” on the ground or 48” flying, and carries the druid and up to 8 other man-sized creatures, who must first be touched by the druid to be able to ride. The druid steers it by spoken command: stop or go, walk, trot, run or fly, turn left or right.

Anyone other than the druid and the chosen passengers who comes within 5’ of the horses or chariot, willingly or not, takes damage as from a wall of fire.
