Damaging it: the chariot is a physical thing and can be damaged, but only by magical weapons or by water (one quart does 1 hit point). The chariot and each horse are armor class 2 and need 30 hit points of damage to dispel. Fire has no effect on them, but magical fires (other than the chariot’s own) do affect riders exposed to them.

Components: mistletoe, a small piece of wood, 2 holly berries, and a fire at least as large as a torch.

Confuses creatures within range for 1 melee round per level of the caster.

Number affected: 2 to 8 creatures, plus the druid’s level minus the level or hit dice of the strongest opponent in range and area (add this if positive, ignore it if negative). The creatures closest to the druid in the area are affected first.

Each round, at the start of the round, every affected creature makes a saving throw at -2, and acts by this table if it fails:

Die RollAction
01–10Wander away for 1 turn
11–60Stand confused for 1 round
61–80Attack nearest creature for 1 round
81–00Attack druid or his party for 1 round

A creature that rolls “wander away for 1 turn” moves as far from the druid as it can in one turn of normal movement, as conditions allow, and makes no saving throws during that turn.

rolls.label: Creatures affected (add the caster's level less the strongest opponent's, if positive)

rows.text: Attack the caster or his or her party for 1 round

system.description: Summons a 16 hit dice earth elemental to do the druid’s bidding. The druid only needs to give it commands and can then act freely, since the elemental has no hostility toward the druid who called it. It stays until destroyed, dispelled, or dismissed (cf. conjure fire elemental).

More powerful than the cleric spell of the same name (q.v.): with greater mistletoe, the druid can change the weather by two places from the prevailing conditions. Otherwise it is the same as the 7th level cleric spell control weather.

rolls.label: Delay before the weather is felt (turns, as the cleric spell)

system.description:
Calls up a mass of 500 to 1000 (d6 + 4, in hundreds) venomous biting and stinging arachnids, insects and myriapods, a carpet 2” square. On the druid’s command it creeps at 1” per round toward any prey within 8”, in the direction commanded.

It kills any creature subject to normal attacks: each creature in the mass does 1 hit point of damage and then dies, so up to 1,000 hit points of damage can be done to creatures in its path. If it goes more than 8” from the summoner, it loses 50 of its number for each 1” beyond 8” (at 10” it has shrunk by 100). There are a number of ways to thwart or destroy the swarm, all of them obvious.

Stops the victim’s heart. The druid speaks the incantation and points his or her index finger at the creature; unless it makes the appropriate saving throw, it dies. A successful saving throw negates the spell.

Fills an area with sheets of roaring flame, each like a wall of fire (q.v.). Creatures inside, or within 1” of the edge, take 2 to 16 hit points of damage plus 1 per level of the druid, or one-half that with a successful saving throw.

The area is 2 cubic ” per level of the druid: a 13th level druid’s fire storm can measure 13” by 2” by 1”. It is 1” or 2” high, with the rest of the volume in length and width.

Reverse (fire quench): smothers normal fires over double the area of a fire storm. Against a magical fire (such as a fire storm) no larger than the normal fire storm area, it has a 5% chance per level of the caster to put it out.

Brings a dead person back in another body, if death occurred no more than a week before casting. The person remembers most of his or her former life and form, but the new incarnation may have a quite different class (if any), and abilities and speech are often changed too. Roll on the table:

Die RollIncarnation
01-03badger
04-08bear, black
09-12bear, brown
13-16boar, wild
17-19centaur
20-23dryad
24-28eagle
29-31elf
32-34faun
35-36fox
37-40gnome
41-44hawk
45-58human
59-61lynx
62-64owl
65-68pixie
69-70raccoon
71-75stag
76-80wolf
81-85wolverine
86-00use magic-user reincarnation table

Any kind of player character can be reincarnated. If the result is an elf, gnome or human, the character must be created anew. When the corpse is touched, the new incarnation appears in the area within 1 to 6 turns. (Cf. the sixth level magic-user spell reincarnation.)

Changes a metal object into wood, up to 80 gold pieces weight of metal per level. Magical metal objects are only 10% likely to be affected. Not even dispel magic reverses the change: a metal door turned to wood stays a wooden door forever.

Makes a small fire, from a torch or lantern up to a normal bonfire of 3’ maximum diameter, either shrink and dim to match-like light or brighten to the brightness of a light spell. Reducing it halves fuel consumption; increasing it doubles consumption. The heat given off does not change either way.

Jets of searing flame shoot from the caster’s fingertips. The thumbs must touch with fingers spread, so the flames form a fan-shaped sheet: jets 3’ long in a horizontal arc of about 120° in front of the caster. Every creature in the flames takes 1 hit point of damage per level of the caster, with no saving throw. Flammable materials touched by the flames burn (cloth, paper, parchment, thin wood, etc.).

Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the second level druid spell charm person or mammal (q.v.), but the magic-user can only charm persons: brownies, dwarves, elves, gnolls, gnomes, goblins, half-elves, halflings, half-orcs, hobgoblins, humans, kobolds, lizard men, nixies, orcs, pixies, sprites and troglodytes. Everything else said about that spell’s effects applies to persons.

system.aoe: One written object or speaking creature
system.description:
The caster can read an otherwise incomprehensible written message, such as a treasure map, or understand a creature’s speech. Magical writing cannot be read, except to know that it is “magic”. The caster must touch the object to be read or the creature to be understood, and cannot write or speak the language.

Components: a pinch of soot and a few grains of salt.

Reverse (confuse languages): prevents comprehension, or cancels a comprehend languages spell.

The caster creates, at his or her choice, either A) 1 to 4 lights like torches and/or lanterns (giving that much light), B) 1 to 4 glowing spheres of light (like will-o-wisps), or C) one faintly glowing, vaguely man-like shape, rather like a creature from the Elemental Plane of Fire. The lights move as the caster wishes, forward or back, straight or around corners, without needing concentration. They wink out if they go beyond the range or the duration runs out.

Range: 4” plus 1” per level. Duration: 2 melee rounds per level. Component: a bit of phosphorus or wytchwood, or a glowworm.
The same as the first level cleric spell detect magic, except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics (duration, area of effect, and no material component).

Makes a single creature or object, which the caster must be able to see, instantly grow in size and weight. Range is ½” per level and duration 1 turn per level.

  • Creatures (including symbiotic or community entities) grow by 20% per level of the caster, to a maximum of 200% extra.
  • Objects grow half as much: 10% per level, to a maximum of 100% extra.
  • Maximum starting volume: 10 cubic feet of living material, or 5 cubic feet of non-living matter, per level.

Magical properties are not increased: a huge +1 sword is still only +1, a staff-sized wand still has only its normal functions, a giant-sized potion just has to be drunk in greater quantity to work, etc. But weight, mass and strength do increase: a table blocking a door is heavier and more effective; a thrown stone has more mass (and hurts more, if enlarged just before impact); chains are more massive; doors thicker; a thin line becomes a sizable, longer rope; and so on. A person 12’ tall would be like an ogre, and one 18’ tall would actually be a giant while the spell lasts.

Reverse (reduce): negates enlarge, or makes creatures or objects smaller by the same ratios.

An unwilling target of either version gets a saving throw; if it succeeds, the spell is wasted.

Component: a pinch of powdered iron.

system.aoe: One scroll or two facing pages
system.description: Removes writing, magical or mundane, from a scroll or from one or two pages or sheets of paper, parchment or similar material. It does not remove explosive runes or a symbol (see those spells). The chance of success is 50% plus 2% per level of the caster for magical writing, or plus 4% per level for mundane writing. This is the writing’s saving throw: a percentile roll above the adjusted chance means the spell fails.

The creatures or objects affected instantly take on the mass of a piece of feathery down. They fall at a constant 2’ per second (12’ per segment) and take no damage on landing while the spell lasts; once it ends, they fall normally.

It can be cast on the caster or any other creature or object within range (1” per level), and lasts 1 segment per level. It affects an area of 1 cubic inch, and the total weight affected cannot exceed 2,000 gold pieces weight plus 2,000 gold pieces weight per level. For example, a 2nd level magic-user has a range of 2”, a duration of 2 segments and a weight limit of 6,000 gold pieces (600 pounds).

It works only on things falling freely or propelled through the air: not on a sword blow or a charging creature, but it does affect a missile.

Component: a small feather or piece of down somewhere on the caster.

A familiar adds to its master’s hit points, shares its senses with him or her, can talk with its master, and serves as a guard, scout and spy. But the magic-user has no control over what kind of creature answers the summons, or whether any comes at all, and the spell can only be tried once per year.

Casting: the magic-user fills a brass brazier with charcoal and, when it is burning well, adds 100 g.p. worth of incense, herbs (certainly basil, savory and catnip) and fat. While these burn, the caster begins the incantation and continues it until the familiar comes or the casting time is over. The referee determines all results secretly:

d20*FamiliarSensory powers
1-4cat, blackexcellent night vision & superior hearing
5-6crowexcellent vision
7-8hawkvery superior distance vision
9-10owl, screechnight vision equal to human daylight vision, superior hearing
11-12toadwide angle vision
13-14weaselsuperior hearing & very superior sense of smell
15special (see below)
16-20*no familiar available within spell range

*Subtract 1 from the roll for each 3 levels of the caster. If the adjusted score is 15 or less, roll again using d16; if a 16 is rolled, that result is final.

Special familiar (a roll of 15), by the magic-user’s alignment:

Alignment of magic-userSpecial familiar
chaotic evil or chaotic neutralquasit (see 1e FRPG, MM)
chaotic good, neutral, or neutral goodpseudo-dragon (see 1e FRPG, MM)
lawful neutral or lawful goodbrownie (see 1e FRPG, MM)
lawful evil or neutral evilimp (see 1e FRPG, MM)

Normal familiars have 2-4 hit points and armor class 7 (from size, speed, etc.). Each is unusually intelligent and totally loyal to its master. Its hit points are added to the magic-user’s total while it is within 12” of its master, but if the familiar is ever killed, the magic-user permanently loses double that number of hit points.

Special familiars: the powers they give are described in 1e Fantasy RPG, MM, except for the brownie. A brownie becomes the magic-user’s friend and companion, and the magic-user gains dexterity equal to the brownie’s (18), is never surprised, and gets +2 on all saving throws. A special familiar gets a saving throw versus magic when summoned; if it succeeds, it ignores the spell, and NO familiar is available to the caster that year.

A familiar will only fight for its master’s life in a life-and-death situation, and imps and quasits are 90% likely not to do so at the risk of their own lives.

Creatures within the area of effect make a saving throw versus magic. To those that fail, the caster’s charisma is temporarily raised by 2-8 points: they are very impressed and want very much to be the caster’s friends and help. To those that succeed, the caster’s charisma is temporarily lowered by 1-4 points: they feel uneasy around the caster and tend to find him or her irritating. The spell has no effect at all on creatures of animal intelligence or lower.

Components: chalk (or white flour), lampblack (or soot) and vermillion, applied to the face before casting.

Magically bars a door, gate or valve of wood, metal or stone, holding it shut as if securely stopped and locked. Range is 2” per level and duration 1 round per level.

Any extra-dimensional creature (demon, devil, elemental, etc.) shatters a held portal. A magic-user four or more levels higher than the caster can open it at will. A knock (q.v.) or dispel magic (q.v.) negates it. A held portal can also be broken or battered down.

The magic-user handles one item to try to learn what dweomer it has. The item must be held or worn in the normal way: a bracelet on the wrist, a helm on the head, boots on the feet, a cloak worn, a dagger held, and so on. The magic-user suffers any consequences of using it, though he or she still gets any saving throw normally allowed. The item must be examined within 1 hour per level of the examiner after it was found, or its impressions blend into those of the characters who have handled it since.

Learning properties: for each segment the spell lasts, there is a 15% + 5% per level chance that 1 property can be learned (possibly that the item has no properties and is merely a ruse, if magic aura or a magic mouth is detected). Each time, the referee secretly rolls the magic-user’s saving throw versus magic: if it succeeds, the property is learned; if it misses by 1 point, a false power is revealed; if it misses by more than 1, nothing is learned.

Limits: the exact bonuses to hit and damage are never revealed, only whether there are few or many. The exact number of charges is never revealed either, only a figure within +/-25% of the actual (a wand with 40 charges might feel like 30, or 50, or anything between).

Cost: after casting, the magic-user loses 8 points of constitution, regaining them at 6 turns of rest per 1 point. If this drops constitution below 3, the caster falls unconscious until full constitution returns 24 hours later.

Components: a pearl (worth at least 100 g.p.) and an owl feather steeped in wine; the infusion is drunk and a live miniature carp swallowed whole before casting. Adding a powdered luckstone to the infusion increases the chance by 25% and gives +4 on all the saving throws.

The recipient can leap up to 30’ forward, or 10’ backward or straight up. Forward and backward leaps follow only a slight arc, about 2’ of height per 10’ of distance. The spell does not make landing, or grabbing hold at the end, any safer.

One leap is granted, plus 1 more for every 3 levels of the caster beyond the 1st: 2 leaps at 4th level, 3 at 7th, etc. All leaps must be made within 1 turn of casting, when the spell wears off.

Component: a grasshopper’s hind leg for each leap, broken as the leap is made.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the first level cleric spell light (q.v.).

system.aoe: One or more creatures in a 10 square foot area
system.description: Magical missiles dart from the caster’s fingertip and strike their target unerringly, each doing 2 to 5 hit points (d4 + 1) of damage. The caster gets one missile, plus one more for every 2 levels: 2 at 3rd level, 3 at 5th, 4 at 7th, etc. Several missiles can hit one creature or several, as the caster wishes. Range is 6” plus 1” per level of the caster.

Repairs small breaks in objects. It welds a broken ring, chain link, medallion or slender dagger, as long as there is only one break. Ceramic or wooden objects with several breaks are invisibly rejoined, as strong as new. A hole in a leather sack or wineskin is completely closed. It does not repair magic items of any kind.

Components: two small magnets of any kind (most likely lodestone) or two burrs.

The caster whispers a message while pointing a finger (secretly or openly), and the message travels in a straight line and can be heard by the creature pointed at. The message must fit within the spell’s duration; if time remains, the creature can whisper a reply that the caster hears. There must be an open, unobstructed path between them.

Component: a short piece of finely drawn copper.

Gives one item, weighing up to 50 g.p. per level of the caster, an aura that shows up if magic is detected on it. If the creature detecting for a dweomer is actually holding the object, it gets a saving throw versus magic; on a success it knows the aura was placed to mislead the unwary. Otherwise the item simply seems magical, and no amount of testing will reveal what the magic is.

Component: a small square of silk, passed over the object.

Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, and the use of powdered iron and silver to trace the magic circle (for protection from evil), this is the same as the first level cleric spell protection from evil (q.v.).

An invisible force strikes whatever object the caster points at. The force is small, 1 foot pound per level of the caster, but it can move small objects up to 1’ directly away from the caster, topple an object in the right conditions, or make a creature lose its balance.

  • Against an attacking creature: if it fails its saving throw, it loses its balance and cannot attack that round. The creature’s mass cannot exceed the force by more than a factor of 50 (a 1st level magic-user cannot effectively push a creature heavier than 50 pounds).
  • Against an object a creature holds: if the creature fails its saving throw versus magic, it subtracts the spell’s force in foot pounds (1, 2, 3, etc.) from its chance to hit, or adds it to its opponents’ saving throws, as applicable.

Component: a small pinch of powdered brass, blown from the palm before pointing at the target.

The magic-user can read magical inscriptions on objects (books, scrolls, weapons and the like) that would otherwise be totally unintelligible. (The magic-user’s own books, and writings already read magically, are already intelligible.) Reading does not normally set off the magic in the writing, though it may with a curse scroll. Once a particular writing has been read this way, the magic-user can read it again later without the spell. Lasts 2 rounds per level.

Component: a clear crystal or mineral prism, which is not used up.

Reverse (unreadable magic): makes the writing completely unreadable to anyone, even with read magic, until the spell wears off or is dispelled. Components: a pinch of dirt and a drop of water.

The caster builds up a powerful electrical charge that jolts the creature touched, doing 1 to 8 hit points of damage (d8) plus 1 per level of the caster (a 2nd level magic-user does 3 to 10). The caster only needs to lay a hand on the opponent’s body, or on an electrical conductor touching it. The opponent touching the caster does not set it off.

Puts one or more creatures into a comatose slumber, except undead and certain other creatures specifically excluded (see 1e Fantasy RPG, MM). All the creatures affected must be within a 3” diameter circle, placed where the caster chooses within range. How many fall asleep depends on their hit dice:

Creature hit diceNumber affected
up to 14-16 (4d4)
1 + 1 to 22-8 (2d4)
2 + 1 to 31-4 (1d4)
3 + 1 to 41-2 (½d4, round off)
4 + 1 to 4 +40-1 (d4: 1 is affected on a 3 or 4)

Slapping or wounding wakes a sleeper, but noise does not; waking takes 1 complete melee round. Sleeping creatures can be killed automatically, 1 per attacker per melee round.

Component: a pinch of fine sand, rose petals, or a live cricket.

Creates an invisible barrier in front of the caster. Against attacks from the front only (where the shield can move to block), it:

  • totally negates magic missile attacks;
  • gives armor class 2 against hand-hurled missiles (axes, darts, javelins, spears, etc.);
  • gives armor class 3 against small device-propelled missiles (arrows, bolts, bullets, manticore spikes, sling stones, etc.);
  • gives armor class 4 against all other attacks;
  • adds +1 to the caster’s saving throws against basically frontal attacks.

The recipient can climb and move on vertical surfaces as a giant spider does, at a movement rate of 3”, and can even hang upside down from ceilings. Hands and feet must be bare. While the spell lasts, objects weighing less than 50 g.p. stick to the recipient’s hands and feet, so a magic-user will find it virtually impossible to cast spells.

Components: a drop of bitumen and a live spider, both eaten by the recipient.

Creates a circular plane of null-gravity. The disc is concave, 3’ across, and holds 1,000 g.p. weight per level of the caster. It always floats about 3’ above the ground and stays level.

If not commanded otherwise, it stays 6’ from the caster. On command it moves anywhere within range, or along with the caster at 6”. If the caster goes beyond range or the spell ends, the disc vanishes and whatever was on it drops to the surface below.

Component: a drop of mercury.

Creates an invisible force that obeys the caster like a valet or butler: it fetches and carries, opens doors, holds chairs, cleans and mends. It is weak, carrying at most 200 gold pieces weight lifted, or twice that pushed across a fairly friction-free surface such as a smooth stone or wood floor, and can only open normal doors, drawers, lids, etc. It cannot fight, and cannot be killed since it is a force, not a creature, but it can be dispelled, or destroyed by 6 hit points of magical damage.

Components: a piece of string and a bit of wood.

The caster makes his or her voice, or another voice or similar sound, seem to come from somewhere else: another creature, a statue, behind a door, down a passage, etc. The voice can be made to sound like a different creature, but only in a language the caster knows, or as a sound the caster can normally make. Each hearer has a 10% chance per point of intelligence above 12 to recognize the trick.

Component: a small cone of parchment.

Lets a magic-user try to copy into his or her spell book a spell he or she cannot yet understand (because of level or not enough intelligence).

Saving throw: to attempt it, the magic-user must save versus magic: at +2 if the spell is no more than 1 level above what he or she can currently use, at 0 for 2 levels higher, and at -1 per level from 3 levels higher on. On a failure, the magic-user takes 1d4 damage per level of the spell and is knocked unconscious for the same number of turns. This damage, if not fatal, heals only at 1-4 points per day, since it harms both mind and body.

Time: copying takes 1 hour per level of the spell, during which the magic-user is in a trance and can always be surprised by any foe.

Components: the writing surface, and a fine ink of rare substances (at least 200 g.p. per bottle, if it can be had at all without the magic-user making it).

rolls.label: Damage if the saving throw fails (also turns unconscious)

system.description:
Creates sound at any distance the caster chooses within range, which can seem to move away, come closer, or stay in place. The volume depends on the caster’s level: at 3rd level (the lowest at which it can be cast), up to the noise of 4 men; each further level adds that much again (up to 8 men at 4th level, and so on). So it can produce talking, singing or shouting, and/or walking, marching or running.

Almost any sound is possible, as long as its volume fits the caster’s level. For comparison: a horde of rats running and squeaking is about as loud as 8 men running and shouting; a roaring lion equals 16 men; a roaring dragon equals no fewer than 24 men.

A character who says he or she disbelieves the sound makes a saving throw; on a success, the character hears nothing, or perhaps a faint sound. The spell works especially well together with phantasmal force (see below).

Component: a bit of wool or a small lump of wax.
The same as the third level cleric spell continual light (q.v.), except that the range is only 6”, not 12”, and the caster cannot reverse it.

Fills the area with total, impenetrable darkness. Infravision and ultravision are useless, and neither normal nor magical light works, except a light or continual light spell: light and darkness negate each other.

Components: a bit of bat fur and either a drop of pitch or a piece of coal.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the first level cleric spell detect evil (q.v.).

The caster clearly sees invisible objects, and astral, ethereal, hidden, invisible or out of phase creatures, in his or her line of sight along a 1” wide path out to the limit of range.

Components: a pinch of talc and a small sprinkling of powdered silver.

The caster can detect the surface thoughts of creatures in range, except creatures with no mind (as we know it), such as all undead. ESP is blocked by 2 or more feet of rock, 2 or more inches of any metal other than lead, or a thin sheet of lead foil.

The caster can probe the surface thoughts of 1 creature per turn, getting only simple instinctive thoughts from lower order creatures, and can keep probing the same creature from round to round. It can help find out whether something lurks behind a door, for example, but will not always reveal what kind of creature it is.

Component: a copper piece.

system.aoe: 1 cubic foot per level of the magic-user
system.description:
For the spell’s duration, copper coins become gold pieces, or brass items become solid gold. A huge amount can be changed; for this spell, assume 4,000 g.p. take up a cubic foot.

Seeing through it: any creature looking at the fools gold gets a saving throw: it must roll equal to or less than its intelligence, adding 1 to its roll for each level of the caster, so gold made by a high level caster is unlikely to be detected.

Cold iron: if the “gold” is struck hard with cold-wrought iron, it may turn back, depending on the material component used:

Component (powdered and sprinkled over the metal)Chance cold iron reveals it
50 g.p. citrine30%
100 g.p. amber25%
500 g.p. topaz10%
1,000 g.p. oriental (corundum) topaz1%

Creatures in the area of effect forget the events of the previous round (the 1 minute before the spell was spoken), plus another minute for every 3 levels of the caster. It does not undo any charm, suggestion, geas, quest or similar spell, but the victim might forget the creature who placed such magic on it.

The caster chooses 1-4 creatures. Against 1, it saves versus magic at -2; against 2, each saves at -1; against 3 or 4, they save normally.

The lost memories can be restored by a cleric’s heal or restoration cast specially for this purpose, or by a wish, but by nothing else.

The recipient vanishes from sight, undetectable by normal vision or even infravision. It is not silenced, so its normal noises can still be heard. Even its allies cannot see it or its gear unless they can normally see invisible things or use magic to do so.

The spell lasts until magically broken or dispelled, until the recipient (or caster) cancels it, or until the recipient attacks any creature. The recipient can open doors, talk, eat, climb stairs, etc., but making any form of attack ends the invisibility at once, although that first attack still benefits from it.

All highly intelligent creatures with 10 or more hit dice or levels of experience, or the equivalent in intelligence/dice/levels, have a chance to automatically detect invisible objects.

Components: an eyelash encased in a bit of gum arabic.

Opens stuck, held or wizard locked doors, and barred or otherwise locked doors. It makes secret doors open, opens locked or trick-opening boxes and chests, and loosens shackles or chains.

Used on a wizard-locked door, it does not remove the wizard lock but suspends it for 1 turn. In all other cases it opens locks or welds permanently, though a lock could be closed and locked again afterwards. It does not raise bars or similar obstacles (such as a portcullis).

One knock performs two of these functions; a door that is locked, barred and held needs two knock spells to open.

A false trap meant to fool dwarves and/or thieves trying to steal the caster’s goods. The caster places the dweomer on any small mechanism, such as a lock, hinge, hasp, screw-on cap, ratchet, etc.

A character able to detect traps who examines it is 80% likely to notice the “trap” and believe it real, less 4% per level of the examiner beyond the first. Someone trying to remove it is only 20% likely to believe he or she has succeeded, plus 4% per level of the remover. It is only an illusion, so nothing happens if it is ignored; its purpose is to frighten thieves away or make them waste precious time.

Only one false trap can be placed in a 50’ by 50’ area. Component: a piece of iron pyrite touched to the object.

The caster can levitate himself or herself, or another creature, up to 1,000 gold pieces weight per level (a third level magic-user can levitate up to 300 pounds, 3,000 g.p.). Cast on himself or herself, the caster can move up or down at 20’ per round; cast on another creature, the caster can move it up or down at up to 10’ per round.

The spell gives no horizontal movement, though the subject could push along a cliff face, for example, to move sideways. The caster can end the spell at will. An unwilling creature gets a saving throw.

Component: a small leather loop, or a piece of golden wire bent into a cup shape with a long shank on one end.
The same as the third level cleric spell locate object (q.v.), except for its range.

An enchanted mouth appears on the chosen object and speaks a message when a specified event happens. The message can be 25 words or less in a language the caster knows, spoken over 1 turn from start to finish; it cannot cast spells. The mouth moves with the words, so on a statue the statue’s mouth would appear to speak. It can be placed on a tree, rock, door or any other object, but not on intelligent animals or plants.

The trigger can be as general or as detailed as the caster likes: “speak to the first creature that touches you”, “to the first creature that passes within 30’”, or even “Speak only when an octogenarian female human carrying a sack of groat clusters sits cross-legged within 1’.” The trigger’s range is ½” per level (a 6th level magic-user’s mouth can respond to an event up to 3” away). The spell lasts until the condition is met.

The mouth cannot detect invisible creatures, alignment, level, hit dice, or class (except by outward dress).

Component: a small bit of honeycomb.

Creates 1 to 4 exact duplicates of the caster around him or her. They copy everything the caster does, and the spell’s blurring and slight distortion make it impossible for opponents to be sure which is real. An image struck by any weapon, magical or not, disappears; the others remain until struck. The images shift around each round, so even if the real caster is hit one round, he or she cannot be picked out the next. All images vanish when the spell ends.

Number of images: roll percentile dice and add 1 per level of the caster: 25 or less = 1 image, 26-50 = 2, 51-75 = 3, over 75 = 4 (printed as “75 or more”).

system.aoe: 10 or 100 times the fire source used
system.description: Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the third level druid spell pyrotechnics (q.v.).

Weakens an opponent, reducing its strength, and the attacks that rely on it, by 25% or more: an extra 2% for each level of the caster beyond the third (27% at 4th level). Range and duration also depend on the caster’s level. A creature struck loses that percentage of the damage it does with physical attacks (missiles, thrusting/cutting/crushing weapons, biting, clawing, goring, kicking, constriction, etc.). The referee decides any other reductions suited to the creature. A successful saving throw negates the spell.

Cast on a rope 5’ to 30’ long, one end rises until the rope hangs straight up as if tied at the top. The top is actually fastened in an extra-dimensional space, where the caster and up to five others can climb up and vanish into a place of safety where no creature can find them. Only one person can climb at a time. Climbers who stop short of the top stay in normal space.

If fewer than six persons have climbed it, the rope can be pulled up into the space; otherwise it simply hangs in the air, staying there unless some creature removes it. Those inside must climb down before the spell ends, or they are dropped from the height they climbed to when it wears off.

Components: powdered corn extract and a twisted loop of parchment.

A creature with fewer than 6 levels of experience/hit dice must save versus magic or fall into a fit of trembling and shaking. It does not drop what it holds unless it is encumbered. If cornered it will fight, but at -1 on “to hit” and damage rolls and on all saving throws.

It has no effect on elves, half-elves, undead (skeletons, zombies, ghouls, shadows, ghasts, wights, wraiths), larvae, lemures, manes, or clerics of any kind.

Component: a bit of bone from an undead skeleton, zombie, ghoul, ghast or mummy.

Affects non-magical objects of crystal, glass, ceramic or porcelain, such as vials, bottles, flasks, jugs, windows, mirrors, etc., shivering them into dozens of pieces. Objects weighing more than 100 gold pieces weight per level of the caster are not affected; all others of these materials must save versus a “crushing blow” or shatter.

Component: a chip of mica.

Creates a billowing mass of nauseating vapor up to 3” from the caster. Any creature caught in it must save versus poison or be helpless with nausea for 2 to 5 rounds (d4 + 1). Those who save are helpless only while they stay inside the cloud and for the round after they leave it, because it irritates the eyes and nose.

Component: a rotten egg or several skunk cabbage leaves.

Raises the character’s strength for the duration, by a number of points, or by tenths of points (percentages) for a fighter who already has 18 strength. The gain depends on class, and all limits on strength from race, sex or class still apply:

ClassStrength gain
Cleric1-6 (d6)
Fighter1-8 (d8)
Magic-user1-4 (d4)
Thief1-6 (d6)
Monk1-4 (d4)

A fighter (or paladin or ranger) who already has 18 strength adds 10% to 80% to his exceptional strength roll. Likewise, any gain that would take strength above 18 counts each 1 point as an extra 10% of exceptional strength.

Component: a few hairs or a pinch of dung from a particularly strong animal (ape, bear, ox, etc.).

Magically locks a door, chest or portal. It can only be opened by breaking it, by dispel magic or knock (qq.v.), or by a magic-user 4 or more levels higher than the caster. The last two do not remove the wizard lock, only suspend it briefly. Extra-dimensional creatures do not affect a wizard lock as they do a held portal (see hold portal).

During each minute (round) the spell lasts, the caster’s body “blinks” out and back onto this plane at a random moment and in a random direction (cf. 1e Fantasy RPG, MM, Blink Dog).

When and where: roll 2d4 for the segment of the round in which the caster blinks out; in that same segment he or she reappears 2’ from the previous position. Roll d8 for direction: 1 = right ahead, 2 = right, 3 = right behind, 4 = behind, 5 = left behind, 6 = left, 7 = left ahead, 8 = ahead.

Blocked space: if something already occupies the arrival space, the caster is moved further away from the round’s starting position as far as needed to reach empty space, but never more than an extra 10’. If even that would put the caster inside another solid object, he or she is trapped on the ethereal plane.

Being attacked: from the blink segment on, the caster can only be hit by attacks that strike both locations at once (a breath weapon, fireball or similar wide area attack). Other opponents can only hit the caster if they attacked before the blink segment.

Acting: the caster is only 75% likely to manage any act other than a physical attack with a hand-held stabbing or striking weapon. Using any spell, device or item might fail, or work incorrectly or in the wrong direction; the referee decides the result for the particular action.

The caster concentrates on a place and hears in his or her mind any noise within a 6” radius of it. Distance does not matter, but the place must be known: familiar to the caster, or obvious (behind a door, around a corner, in a copse of woods, etc.). Only sounds the caster could normally hear are heard. Only metal sheeting or magical protections block the spell. It works only on the plane the caster is on when casting.

Component: a small silver horn worth at least 100 g.p., which disappears when the spell is cast.

Creates a many-layered mass of strong, sticky strands like spider webs, but far larger and tougher. The mass must be anchored between two or more opposite points (floor and ceiling, opposite walls, etc.). It covers up to 8 cubic inches and must be at least 1” thick, so a mass 4” high, 2” wide and 1” deep can be made.

Getting stuck: creatures inside the web, or simply touching it, are stuck in the gluey fibers. The saving throw is made at -2. A creature that saves has jumped free if it has room to escape; if there is no room, the webs are only ½ strength against it.

StrengthBreaking free
less than 13stuck until freed by another or until the spell ends; 5% cumulative chance per full turn of suffocating to death
13 to 17breaks through 1’ of web per turn
18 or morebreaks through 1’ of web per round
strong and huge creaturesbreak through 1’ of web per segment

(Enough mass counts as great strength here; very massive creatures hardly notice webs.)

Fire: the strands are flammable. A magic flaming sword slashes them away as easily as a hand brushes away cobwebs. Any fire (torch, flaming oil, flaming sword, etc.) sets them alight and burns them away in a single round; every creature still in the webs takes 2-8 hit points of damage from the flames, but those already free are not harmed.

Component: a bit of spider web.

Like clairaudience, but the caster sees in his or her mind whatever is within sight of the chosen place. Distance does not matter, but the place must be known (familiar or obvious). Light matters, even if the caster can see infrared or ultraviolet: in darkness only a 1” radius around the centre of the place can be seen; otherwise sight extends to normal vision range. Metal sheeting or magical protections block the spell. It works only on the plane the caster is on when casting.

Component: a pinch of powdered pineal gland from a human or humanoid creature.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the third level cleric spell dispel magic (q.v.).

Mystic runes traced on a book, map, scroll or similar written item prevent unauthorized reading. They are hard to detect: 5% per level of magic-use experience of the reader, and thieves have only a 5% chance in any case.

When read, the runes explode: the reader takes the full 12 to 30 (6d4 + 6) hit points of damage with no saving throw, and creatures within the blast radius take the same, or half on a successful saving throw. The item is destroyed in the explosion unless it is normally immune to destruction by magical fire.

The caster, and any other magic-users he or she instructs, can use the item without setting off the runes, and the caster can remove them at will. Otherwise only dispel magic removes them. They last until triggered.

Puts the caster, or any other willing creature whose levels/hit dice do not exceed the caster’s level, into a cataleptic state that cannot be told apart from real death. The subject can smell, hear and know what is happening, but cannot feel or see anything, so wounds or mistreatment are not felt, cause no reaction, and do only one-half normal damage.

Paralysis, poison and energy level drain do not affect the subject while the spell lasts. Poison injected or otherwise put into the body takes effect when the spell ends, though a saving throw is allowed.

The caster can end the spell at any time, but it takes 1 full round for the body to start working again.

An explosive burst of flame that goes off with a low roar, doing 1 six-sided die (d6) of damage per level of the caster. Exceptions: fireball wands do 6 dice (6d6), staves with this power do 8 dice, and fireball scrolls do 5 to 10 dice (d6 + 4).

Casting: the caster points and states the range (distance and height) where the fireball is to burst. A streak flashes from the finger and blossoms into the fireball at that point, unless it hits a material body first.

Area: the burst has little pressure and generally fills the shape of the space it is in, covering an area equal to its normal spherical volume [roughly 33,000 cubic feet (or yards) in total].

Damage: creatures that fail their saving throws take full damage. Every creature in the blast that saves dodges, drops flat or rolls aside, taking ½ damage. The fireball also ignites all combustibles within its burst radius, and its heat melts soft metals such as gold, copper, silver, etc. Items exposed to it must be rolled for to see if they are affected; items carried by a creature that makes its saving throw are unaffected.

Component: a tiny ball of bat guano and sulphur.

For the spell’s duration, the caster can touch one arrow or crossbow bolt (quarrel) per segment. Each one touched becomes magical, though with no bonus “to hit”, and must be shot within 1 round, after which the flame consumes it entirely and the magic is lost. Flaming missiles have the normal chances of starting fires, and any creature subject to extra fire damage takes +1 hit point of damage from each one that hits it.

Components: a drop of oil and a small piece of flint.

The recipient can fly, moving up, down and/or sideways at 12” per move (half that climbing, twice that diving). The caster never knows the exact duration, because the Dungeon Master secretly rolls the extra 1-6 turns.

Component: a wing feather of any bird.

rolls.label: Duration (turns; the DM rolls the 1-6 secretly)

system.description:
A strong puff of air blows from the caster in the direction he or she faces, along a path 1” wide and 1” long per level (8” for an 8th level magic-user).

  • Puts out candles, torches and similar unprotected flames.
  • Makes protected flames (such as lanterns) dance wildly, with a 5% chance per level of the caster of putting them out too.
  • Fans large fires 1’ to 6’ outward in the wind’s direction.
  • Forces small flying creatures back 1” to 6”, holds man-sized flying creatures motionless if they try to move against it, and slows large flying creatures by 50% for 1 round.
  • Blows over light objects.

Component: a legume seed.

Affected creatures move and attack at double their normal rate: a creature moving 6” and attacking 1 time per round moves 12” and attacks 2 times per round. Spell casting is not faster. The caster can affect one creature per level, those closest to the caster first, all within the area of effect. Haste negates a slow spell (see hereafter). Because it speeds up the body’s processes, it also ages the recipients.

Component: a shaving of licorice root.

Like the second level cleric spell hold person (q.v.), this immobilizes creatures within range chosen by the caster. Against three or four persons, saving throws are normal; against two, each saves at -1; against one, the save is at -3.

If the spell is partly negated (as a ring of spell turning might do), it acts as a slow spell (q.v.) unless the saving throw succeeds.

Affected creatures: brownies, dryads, dwarves, elves, gnolls, gnomes, goblins, half-elves, halflings, half-orcs, hobgoblins, humans, kobolds, lizard men, nixies, orcs, pixies, sprites and troglodytes.

The recipient can see light in the infrared spectrum, seeing differences in heat radiation up to 6” away. Strong heat sources (fire, lanterns, torches, etc.) tend to dazzle or cast “shadows”, just as bright light does to normal vision, so infravision does not work well near them. Invisible creatures usually cannot be seen with infravision, since invisibility affects infrared light just as it does normal and ultraviolet light.

Component: a pinch of dried carrot or an agate.

Essentially the same as invisibility (q.v.), but for everyone in the area. Those affected cannot see each other. A creature that attacks becomes visible itself, but the others stay invisible unless the spell recipient breaks the spell.

Creates an opaque sphere of force around the caster, half above the ground or floor and the lower half passing through it, so the interior is a hemisphere.

  • Temperature: inside stays at 70° F. while the outside is anywhere from 0° F. to 105° F. Below 0°, the inside drops 1° for each 1° of extra cold; above 105°, it rises likewise.
  • Wind: it withstands winds up to 50 m.p.h.; stronger wind destroys it.
  • Light: the caster can dimly light the inside, or put the light out, on command.
  • Vision: opaque from outside, transparent from inside.
  • No protection from missiles, weapons, spells and the like.

Up to 6 other man-sized creatures fit inside with the caster and can go in and out freely without harming it, but if the caster leaves, the spell ends.

Component: a small crystal bead, which shatters when the spell ends or the hut is dispelled.

Releases a powerful stroke of electrical energy that does 1 six-sided die (d6) of damage per level of the caster to creatures in its area, or 50% of that to those who save.

Range and shape: the range is where the stroke begins; it then extends further from that point. The caster chooses either a forked bolt 1” wide and 4” long, or a single bolt ½” wide and 8” long. If a 12th level magic-user casts it at maximum range, 16”, it starts at 16” and ends at 20” (forked) or 24” (single).

Rebound: if a non-conducting barrier (such as a stone wall) stops the bolt before its full length, it doubles back toward the caster, so its total length from start to end is still the normal amount (regardless of any damage to the barrier). Example: an 8” stroke is started at 4” range, but there is only 3½” of space in that direction, so the bolt starts at the 3½” maximum and rebounds 8” back toward its caster.

Objects: it sets fire to combustibles, splits wooden doors, splinters up to 1’ thickness of stone, and melts metals with a low melting point (lead, gold, copper, silver, bronze). Objects that take the full force of the stroke must make saving throws (cf. fireball).

Components: a bit of fur and an amber, crystal or glass rod.

Within 1-4 rounds of casting, 2-8 first level monsters appear wherever the caster wants within range. The referee picks the monster at random; the number may be rolled or chosen by the referee to suit how strong the monster is. They attack the caster’s opponents as well as they can until the caster tells them to stop, the spell ends, or they are slain. If there is no one to fight, they can perform other services for the caster, if they can communicate and are physically able.

Components: a tiny bag and a small candle (not necessarily lit).

Creates a visual illusion (with no sound) of any object, creature or force, within the spell’s area of effect; the area can be moved within range. It affects every creature that sees and believes it, even to the point of taking damage from illusory missiles or from falling into an illusory pit full of sharp spikes. Creatures that have not seen it are immune until they do.

The illusion lasts until an opponent strikes it (unless the caster makes it react appropriately) or until the caster stops concentrating (by choice, by moving, or because a successful attack damages him or her).

A creature that disbelieves gets a saving throw. If it succeeds, it sees the illusion for what it is, and gives its companions +4 on their saving throws if it can tell them effectively.

Component: a bit of fleece.
The same as the first level spell protection from evil, except for its area of effect. See also the first level cleric spell protection from evil for general information.

The recipient is completely immune to hurled and shot missiles such as arrows, axes, bolts, javelins, small stones and spears. Large and/or magical missiles, such as ballista bolts, catapult stones and magical arrows, bolts, javelins, etc., do 1 less damage per die. It gives no protection against magical attacks such as fireballs, lightning bolts or magic missiles.

Component: a piece of tortoise or turtle shell.

Affected creatures move and attack at one-half their normal or current rate. It negates haste (q.v.), stacks if cast on creatures already slowed, and otherwise affects magically speeded or slowed creatures. It affects one creature per level of the caster, all within the 4” × 4” area centred where the caster directs.

Component: a drop of treacle.

The caster influences the target by speaking a few words (a phrase, or a sentence or two) suggesting a course of action. The target must understand the language. The suggestion must be worded to make the action sound reasonable: asking the creature to stab itself, throw itself onto a spear, set itself on fire, or do anything obviously harmful automatically breaks the spell.

But suggesting that a pool of acid is really pure water and a quick dip would be refreshing is another matter; so is urging a red dragon that it would profit from stopping its attack on the party, since together they could loot a rich treasure elsewhere. A suggestion can stay in effect a long time, as with that red dragon.

A successful saving throw negates the spell. A very reasonable suggestion may impose a penalty on the save (such as -1, -2, etc.) at the Dungeon Master’s discretion. Undead are not affected.

Components: a snake’s tongue and either a bit of honeycomb or a drop of sweet oil.

Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the fourth level cleric spell tongues (q.v.). Component: a small clay model of a ziggurat, which shatters when the spell is spoken.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, and the material component (a short reed or piece of straw), this is the same as the third level druid spell water breathing (q.v.).

Like charm person (q.v.), but it affects any living creature, or several weaker ones: 2-8 1st level creatures, 1-4 2nd level creatures, 1 or 2 3rd level creatures, or 1 creature of 4th or higher level. An affected creature sees the caster as a friend, ally or companion to be treated well and protected. If they can communicate, it follows reasonable requests, instructions or orders very faithfully (cf. suggestion).

Charmed creatures eventually break free. The chance each week depends on the creature’s level or hit dice:

Monster level or hit diceChance per week of breaking the spell
1st or up to 25%
2nd or up to 3 + 210%
3rd or up to 4 + 415%
4th or up to 625%
5th or up to 7 + 235%
6th or up to 8 + 445%
7th or up to 1060%
8th or up to 1275%
9th or over 1290%

Overtly hostile acts by the caster automatically break the spell, or at least give the monster a new saving throw against it.

Makes an ordinary weapon magical: it counts as a +1 weapon but has no bonuses at all. Arrows, axes, bolts, bows, daggers, hammers, maces, spears, swords, etc. can be enchanted: two small weapons (arrows, bolts, daggers, etc.) or one large one (axe, bow, hammer, mace, etc.). An enchanted missile that hits loses the enchantment; otherwise it lasts for the duration based on the caster’s level (40 rounds, or 4 turns, for an 8th level magic-user).

Components: powdered lime and carbon.

Extends the duration of a first, second or third level spell already cast by 50%: a levitate can be made to last 1½ turns/level, a hold person 3 rounds/level, etc. It only works on spells where duration matters.

system.aoe: 6” long cone, 3” diameter at end, ½’ at base
system.description:
An invisible ray makes creatures in its area turn and flee from the caster in panic, at their fastest rate, for as many melee rounds as the caster has levels. The panic begins the round after casting, but they drop what they are holding at once. Creatures that make their saving throws are not affected.

Dropping items: 60% chance at 1st level (or 1 hit die), less 5% per level (or hit die) above that: 15% at 10th level, 0% at 13th.

Component: the heart of a hen or a white feather.

A normal fire, such as a brazier, flambeau or bonfire, becomes a magical agent: a gossamer veil of many-colored flame circles the fire 5’ away. Any creature watching the fire or the circle of flame must save versus magic or be charmed, standing motionless and gazing at the flames. While charmed it is subject to suggestions of 12 or fewer words, and saves against them at -3.

The charm breaks when the creature is physically attacked, when a solid object blocks its view of the flames, or when the spell ends. The veil is not magical fire: passing through it does the same type and amount of damage as passing through the original fire.

Component: a small, exceptionally thin piece of multicolored silk, thrown into the fire.

Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is identical to the seventh level druid spell confusion (q.v.), except that it affects a basic 2-16 creatures. Component: a set of three nut shells.

rolls.label: Creatures affected (add the caster's level less the strongest opponent's, if positive)

rows.text: Attack the caster or his or her party for 1 round

system.aoe: 5’ cube per level of the magic-user
system.description:
Excavates 125 cubic feet of earth, sand or mud per round, a cube 5’ on a side, with the removed material scattered evenly around the pit.

Collapse: digging deeper than 5’ risks collapse: 15% per additional 5’ of depth in earth, 35% in sand, 55% in mud.

Falling in: a creature at the edge (within 1’) of the pit avoids falling in if it rolls its dexterity score or less. A creature moving quickly toward the pit falls in unless it saves versus magic. A creature in the middle of where the pit is dug always falls in.

Components: a miniature shovel and tiny bucket, which the caster must keep holding while each pit is dug.

The caster instantly teleports up to 3” per level, with no chance of error, arriving exactly where intended, either by picturing the spot (within range) or by stating a direction, such as “30 inches straight downwards” or “upwards to the northwest, 45 degree angle, 42 inches.”

  • Arriving in a space already occupied by a solid body leaves the caster in the Astral Plane, stunned and unable to cast spells, until some helpful creature finds him or her and casts dispel magic.
  • Arriving in mid-air with nothing underfoot (when distances are stated) means falling and damage, unless other magic is used.
  • Everything the caster wears or carries goes along, up to 5,000 gold pieces weight of non-living matter, or half that of living matter.

Recovering from the spell takes 7 segments.

The caster seems to burst into flame, but the flames are thin and wispy, giving only half the light of a normal torch (15’ radius of dim light). They are blue or green for variation A, violet or blue for variation B. Any creature that hits the caster with its body or a hand-held weapon does normal damage to the caster, but takes double that amount of damage itself! The other effects depend on the variation:

A) Hot flames: the caster saves against cold-based attacks at +2, taking half damage or none. Fire-based attacks are normal, but if the caster fails the required saving throw (if any) against one, he or she takes double normal damage. Component: a bit of phosphorous.

B) Cold flames: the caster saves against fire-based attacks at +2, taking half damage or none. Cold-based attacks are normal, but if the caster fails the required saving throw (if any) against one, he or she takes double normal damage. Component: a live firefly or glow worm, or the tail parts of 4 dead ones.

Traps any item that closes (book, box, bottle, chest, coffer, coffin, door, drawer and so forth). When the trap goes off, it explodes in a 5’ radius. Every creature in the area makes a saving throw versus magic, taking 1-4 hit points plus 1 per level of the caster, or one-half that on a successful save. The trapped item itself is NOT harmed.

Other spells on the same item:

  • Fire trap and hold portal: only the first one cast works, and the other is negated (both are negated if cast at the same time).
  • Fire trap cast after a wizard lock: the fire trap is negated. Cast at the same time: both negated. Wizard lock cast after a fire trap: 50% chance both are negated.
  • Knock does not affect a fire trap at all; the trap goes off as soon as the intruder opens or touches the item.

The caster can use the item without setting it off. A fire trap is only half as likely as normal to be detected, and a failed attempt to remove it sets it off immediately.

Component: the caster traces the outline of the closure with a bit of sulphur or saltpeter.

The target suddenly becomes clumsy and awkward. Running creatures trip and fall; those reaching for an item fumble and drop it; those using weapons drop them too. Getting up, or picking up the dropped object, usually takes the whole of the next melee round. Breakable items may be damaged when dropped. If the target makes its saving throw, it instead operates at one-half normal efficiency (cf. slow).

Component: a dab of solidified milk fat.

An illusion hides the real terrain in the area. Open fields or a road can be made to look like swamp, hills, a crevasse or other difficult or impassable ground; a pond can look like a grassy meadow, a cliff like a gentle slope, or a rock-strewn gully like a wide, smooth road. The illusion lasts until dispel magic is cast on the area or an intelligent creature touches it. The area grows with level: up to 10” × 10” at 10th level, 12” × 12” at 12th.

Components: a stone, a twig, and a bit of green plant (a leaf or blade of grass).

The caster chooses one of two effects:

  • Hail: great hailstones pound a 4” diameter area, doing 3 to 30 (3d10) hit points of damage to every creature in it.
  • Sleet: driving sleet falls over an 8” diameter area for the duration. Creatures in it are blinded, and the icy ground slows movement by 50%, with a 50% chance that a creature trying to move slips and falls.

This spell negates heat metal (q.v.), but its first use also does damage while doing so.

Components: a pinch of dust and a few drops of water.

Makes willing creatures of man-size or smaller, up to 10 per level of the caster, look like normal trees of any kind, so a company of troops can look like a copse, grove or orchard. Other creatures can pass through and even touch them without discovering the illusion, but blows reveal the truth, since the creatures struck take damage and bleed. All must be in the area of effect; unwilling creatures are not affected. The spell lasts until the caster ends it or dispel magic is cast on the creatures.

Component: a handful of bark chips.

Creates a magical sphere around the caster that no first, second or third level spell can enter: the area of such spells does not include the globe. Spells of any level can be cast out of the globe, passing through it to their targets without affecting it. Fourth and higher level spells are not stopped. Dispel magic can bring it down.

Component: a glass or crystal bead.
Like the third level spell monster summoning I (q.v.), but it conjures 1-6 second level monsters. The material components are the same, and there is also a 1-4 round delay.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the third level druid spell plant growth (q.v.).

A powerful magic that completely changes the target’s form and abilities, and possibly its personality and mind. A creature cannot be turned into something more intelligent than itself, though the reverse is possible.

Survival: the target must make a “system shock” roll (cf. CONSTITUTION) to survive the change. If it does, it gains all the form and abilities of its new shape.

Becoming the new creature: the chance that its personality and mind also change to those of the new form starts at 100%. Subtract 5% per point of the target’s intelligence, and adjust by 5% for each hit die of difference between its own hit dice (or level, for characters) and those of the new form: plus if the new form has more, minus if fewer. Check daily until the change happens. (All creatures generally prefer their own form and will not willingly risk this spell!)

Example: a one hit die orc of 8 intelligence turned into a 6 hit dice white dragon is 85% (100% - [5% × 8 intelligence] + [(6 - 1) × 5%] = 85%) likely to become one in every respect. Either way it has the dragon’s physical and mental capabilities, and if it does not take on the dragon’s personality and mind, it still knows what it knew before. Likewise, an 8th level fighter turned into a blue dragon, if he did not take on the dragon’s mind, would still know weapon combat and could use weapons in the dragon’s grasping forepaws.

The new form may be tougher than it looks: a mummy turned into a puppy would be very tough, and a brontosaurus turned into an ant could not be squashed by a small or even man-sized creature stepping on it.

Returning the creature to its own form requires the magic-user to use dispel magic, which also requires a “system shock” saving throw.

Component: a caterpillar cocoon.

The caster takes the form of any creature, from as small as a wren to as large as a hippopotamus, along with its way of moving. The caster does not gain the creature’s other abilities (attacks, magic, etc.), and there is no risk of changing personality or mind, so no “system shock” check is needed. A magic-user turned into an owl could fly but would still have human vision; as a black pudding he or she could move under doors or along halls and ceilings, but would not have the pudding’s attacks or defenses. The new form must be strong enough to move normally.

The caster can change form as often as desired, each change taking only 5 segments. Damage to the new form counts as damage to the caster, but when he or she returns to normal form, 1 to 12 (d12) points of damage are restored.

rolls.label: Restored on returning to normal form

system.description:
Lets the magic-user memorize, or keep in memory, three extra spell levels: three first level spells, or one first and one second, or one third level spell. The magic-user can either memorize extra spells at once, or use the enhancer to keep the memory of a spell after casting it.

Components: a piece of string, an ivory plaque worth at least 100 g.p., and an ink made of squid secretion and either black dragon’s blood or giant slug digestive juice. All are used up when the spell is cast.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the third level cleric spell remove curse (q.v.).

The same as the fifth level druid spell wall of fire (q.v.), except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics and these: the flames are violet or reddish blue; base damage is 2-12 hit points (plus 1 per level); a ring-shaped wall has a radius of 1” + ¼” per level of the caster; and the material component is phosphorus.

Creates a sheet of strong, flexible ice, mainly for defense, such as stopping pursuers. It is one inch thick per level of the caster and covers a 1” square area per level: a 10th level magic-user could make a wall up to 10” long and 1” high, or 5” long and 2” high, and so forth.

Breaking through does 2 hit points of damage per inch of thickness; fire-using creatures take 3 per inch, cold-using creatures only 1.

Cast as a horizontal sheet falling on opponents, it acts like an ice storm’s (q.v.) hailstones over the area where it falls.

Magical fires such as fireballs and fiery dragon breath melt it in 1 round, creating a great cloud of steamy fog that lasts 1 turn. Normal fires and lesser magical ones do not make it melt any faster.

Component: a small piece of quartz or similar rock crystal.

Creates an invisible sensory organ that sends what it sees to the caster. It moves at 3” per round looking ahead as a human would, or 1” per round examining the ceiling, walls and floor ahead as well as glancing at the walls further on. It sees with infravision up to 10’, or up to 60’ in brightly lit areas, and can travel in any direction while the spell lasts.

Component: a bit of bat fur.

Turns normal liquid, such as water or water-based infusions or solutions, into a less dense substance that can be breathed. A magic-user wanting to reach an underwater place could step into the water, cast the spell and sink down in a globe of bubbling water, in which the caster and any companions inside can move freely and breathe as if it were air. The globe moves with the caster.

Water breathing creatures avoid the sphere (or hemisphere). Intelligent ones can enter it if they can move by some means other than swimming, but no water-breather can breathe inside it.

Only one word is needed to cast it. Component: a small handful of alkaline or bromine salts.

system.aoe: Up to 8 animals in a 2” square area
system.description: Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, and the material component (a pinch of powdered bone), this is the same as the fifth level druid spell animal growth (q.v.).
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the third level cleric spell animate dead (q.v.).

A large to huge disembodied magic hand appears and places itself between the caster and a chosen opponent. It stays between them whatever the caster does afterwards and however the opponent tries to get around it. The caster picks its size, anywhere from human-sized up to titan-sized. It takes as many hit points of damage to destroy as the caster has. Any creature weighing less than 2,000 pounds that tries to push past it is slowed to one-half normal movement.

Component: a glove.

Creates a billowing cloud of ghastly yellowish green vapor, so toxic that:

  • creatures with fewer than 4 + 1 hit dice die;
  • creatures with 4 + 1 to 5 + 1 hit dice must save versus poison at -4 or die;
  • creatures with up to 6 hit dice (inclusive) must save versus poison normally or die.

The cloud rolls along the ground away from the caster at 1” per round. Wind can change its course, but it will not move back toward the caster. A strong wind breaks it up in 4 rounds, and a stronger wind makes the spell impossible to use. Very thick vegetation disperses it in two rounds (2” of movement through it). The vapor is heavier than air, so it sinks to the lowest ground and even pours down den or sinkhole openings, which makes it ideal for wiping out nests of giant ants, for example.

Actually four spells in one: the caster can conjure an air, earth, fire or water elemental, if he or she has the right material component. The type must be chosen before memorizing the spell. A large fire must be within range to conjure a fire elemental, and a large amount of water for a water elemental. A caster who has memorized two or more of these spells can conjure several elementals of different types, one after another.

Conjured elementals are very strong (see 1e Fantasy RPG, MM), typically 16 hit dice (16d8). Each stays until its form on this plane is destroyed by damage or the spell ends. A water elemental is destroyed if it moves more than 6” from a body of water.

Control: the caster must concentrate on the elemental carrying out his or her commands, at a distance of up to 3” per level, or it turns on the caster and attacks. (It will not break off a fight to do so, and it avoids other creatures while seeking its conjurer.) Being wounded or grappled breaks the caster’s concentration. Even with concentration, there is always a 5% chance that the elemental turns on its conjurer, checked at the end of the second round and every round after.

Material components (besides the element itself), a small amount of:

  • Air elemental: burning incense
  • Earth elemental: soft clay
  • Fire elemental: sulphur and phosphorus
  • Water elemental: water and sand

N.B. A pentacle, pentagram, thaumaturgic triangle, magic circle or protection from evil spell gives special protection from uncontrolled elementals.

A cone of cold spreads from the caster’s hand, ½” long per level. It drains heat, doing 1 four-sided die plus 1 hit point of damage (1d4 + 1) per level of the caster: a 10th level magic-user’s cone does 10d4 + 10.

Component: a very small crystal or glass cone.

The caster sends his or her mind to another plane to get advice and information from powers there. These powers are found at random and resent being contacted, so they give only brief answers (the DM answers each question with “yes”, “no”, “maybe”, “never”, “irrelevant”, etc.). The caster can ask one question for every 2 levels, and can contact an elemental plane or some plane further away. The further away the plane, the greater the risk of insanity or death, but the more likely the power is to know the answer and to tell the truth:

PlaneInsanity*KnowledgeVeracity**
Elemental20%90%***75%
1 removed5%60%65%
2 removed10%65%67%
3 removed15%70%70%
4 removed20%75%73%
5 removed25%80%75%
6 removed30%85%78%
7 removed35%90%81%
8 removed40%95%85%
9 or more removed50%98%90%

* Each point of intelligence over 15 lowers the chance of insanity by 5%.

** If the power does not know the answer and the veracity roll says it lies, it gives a definite answer anyway; if the roll says it tells the truth, it answers “unknown.”

*** For questions about the appropriate elemental plane.

Insanity strikes as soon as 1 question is asked, and lasts 1 week per plane of removal (10 weeks at most). There is a 1% chance per plane that the magic-user dies before recovering, unless remove curse is cast on him or her.
The same as the fourth level spell extension I, but it extends the duration of first through fourth level spells by 50%.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the sixth level druid spell feeblemind (q.v.). Component: a handful of small clay, crystal, glass or mineral spheres.

Immobilizes one to four creatures of any type within range and in sight of the caster, who chooses how many. Against three or four, each saves normally; against two, each saves at -1; against one, the save is at -3. A partly negated hold monster acts as a slow spell.

Component: one hard metal bar or rod per monster, which can be as small as a three-penny nail.

The chests: the magic-user needs an exceptionally well-made, expensive chest built by master craftsmen. If mainly wood, it must be ebony, rosewood, sandalwood, teak or the like, with all corner fittings, nails and hardware of platinum. An ivory chest may have gold fittings; a bronze, copper or silver chest may have electrum or silver fittings. Such a chest never costs less than 5,000 g.p. A tiny replica, of the same materials and perfect in every detail, must then be made. A magic-user can have only one pair of these chests at a time, and even wish spells cannot change this!

Casting: touching the chest and holding the replica, the caster chants the spell, and the large chest vanishes into the ethereal plane. It holds one cubic foot per level of the caster, whatever its apparent size. Living matter inside makes the spell 75% likely to fail, so the chest is usually used to protect valuable spell books, magic items, gems, etc. As long as the caster has the replica, he or she can call the chest back to wherever he or she is. If the replica is lost or destroyed, nothing, not even a wish, will bring the chest back.

Risks on the ethereal plane: each week there is a 1% cumulative chance that some creature/being finds the chest. If so: 10% it is ignored, 10% something is added, 30% the contents are exchanged for something else, 30% something is stolen, 20% it is emptied.

Recall: bringing the chest back to the Prime Material Plane opens an ethereal window that stays open for 5 hours, slowly shrinking. There is a 5% chance that some ethereal monster is drawn through it, less 1% (cumulative) each hour after, until the window closes. No creature on the Prime Material Plane can locate the chest, even with a gem of seeing, true seeing, etc.

Duration: if the chest is not retrieved before the spell ends, there is a cumulative 5% chance per day that it is lost forever: 5% at 61 days, 10% at 62 days, and so forth.

Can only be cast while the magic-user has an earth elemental conjured; the elemental does not mind cooperating once the caster announces the intent to cast distance distortion. The spell places the elemental in the area, which is then distorted in one of two ways: 1) distances seem one-half as long to those crossing it, or 2) twice as long. A 10’ × 100’ corridor could seem only 5’ wide and 50’ long, or 20’ wide and 200’ long. When the spell ends, the elemental returns to its own plane.

Creatures travelling through the area cannot detect the distortion at all, though the area radiates a dim dweomer, and true seeing reveals an earth elemental spread through it.

Component: a small lump of soft clay.

The magic-user takes over a victim’s mind and controls its body. If the body is human or humanoid, the magic-user can even cast the spells he or she knows. The possessor can draw on the victim’s basic knowledge but not its real knowledge, so will not know the victim’s language or spells.

The jar: the caster moves his or her life force into a special container (a large gem or crystal), which is the spell’s material component and must be within spell range of the caster’s body when cast. From the jar, the life force can sense and attack any creature within range, but cannot tell what kind of creature it is.

  • Each possession attempt takes 1 round and works only if the victim fails its saving throw; a failure leaves the caster’s life force in the jar.
  • If the caster’s body is destroyed, the life force in the jar is unharmed. If the jar is destroyed, the life force is snuffed out.
  • Returning to the real body takes 1 round, and only from a jar within spell range of the body.

Saving throw: compare the combined intelligence and wisdom of caster and victim (intelligence only for non-human, non-humanoid creatures). Caster’s total minus victim’s total gives the difference; a negative number means the victim scores higher, which gives a bonus:

DifferenceDie Adjustment
Negative 9 or ++4
Negative 8 to 6+3
Negative 5 to 3+2
Negative 2 to 0+1
Positive 1 to 40
Positive 5 to 8-1
Positive 9 to 12-2
Positive 13 or +-3

Fighting back: a possessed creature gets saving throws to push out the possessor’s mind: each round if the difference is negative or a positive number less than 5; each turn for a positive difference of 5 to 8; each day for 9 to 12; each week for 13 or better. If it regains control, the magic-user is trapped until he or she retakes control or escapes.
Summons 1-4 third level monsters, arriving within 1-4 rounds. See monster summoning I for other details.

Summons a phantom watchdog that only the caster can see, and which the caster can set to guard a passage, room, door or similar space or portal. It starts barking loudly as soon as any creature larger than a cat approaches. It can detect invisible, astral, ethereal, out of phase, duo-dimensional and similar unseen creatures, which makes it an excellent guard.

If an intruder turns its back to the hound, the hound attacks viciously as a 10 hit dice monster, doing 3-18 hit points of damage, and can hit any opponent, even those normally hit only by +3 or better magical weapons. The hound cannot be attacked, but it can be dispelled. If the caster is ever more than 3” from the area it guards, the spell ends automatically.

Components: a tiny silver whistle, a piece of bone and a thread.

Opens a passage through a wooden, plaster or stone wall, 5’ wide by 8’ high by 10’ deep, so the caster and companions can simply walk through. Several of these spells together make a continuing passage, so very thick walls can be pierced.

Component: a pinch of sesame seeds.

Shapes an existing piece of stone to suit the caster: making a stone weapon, a special trapdoor, a sculpted idol, or reshaping a stone door to escape imprisonment, as long as the volume of stone is within the area of effect. Stone coffers, secret doors, etc. can be made, but fine detail is not possible.

Component: soft clay, worked roughly into the shape wanted and touched to the stone as the spell is spoken.

The caster moves objects by concentrating on moving them mentally, vertically or horizontally. The speed doubles each round: 2” the first round, 4” the second, 8” the third, 16” the fourth, and so on, up to a maximum of 1,024” per round. (Heavy objects moving at high speed can be deadly weapons!)

It can move opponents within its weight limit, but they can easily counter it with something as simple as an enlarge spell (pushing their weight over the limit). Walking, or some other way of moving under their own power if they cannot walk, also counters it, as long as the speed has not yet reached 16” per round. The various hand spells, and many other magics, also counter it.

The caster instantly travels, along with extra weight being worn or touched, to a well known destination. Distance does not matter, but the spell cannot cross planes. The weight limit is 2,500 g.p., plus 1,500 g.p. for each level above the 10th (a 13th level magic-user can teleport up to 7,000 g.p., or 700 pounds).

Accuracy depends on how well the caster knows the destination. A very familiar place (one the caster has a clear picture of from being there and studying it) is unlikely to go wrong. Lesser known places (seen only by magic or from a distance) are riskier, and unfamiliar places are quite dangerous:

Destination isHighOn targetLow
