High: the caster arrives 1” above the ground for every 1% the roll is below the lowest “On Target” number: at most 2” for a very familiar place, and up to 32” for a place never seen.

Low: if the area arrived in is solid, the caster dies instantly.

It is not possible to teleport into empty space; there must be a substantial surface there, such as a wooden floor, stone floor, natural ground, etc.

Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, and the material components (clay and water; sand, lime and water for the reverse), this is the same as the fifth level druid spell transmute rock to mud (q.v.).

Creates an invisible barrier wherever the caster wishes within range. It does not move, and no spell affects it, not even dispel magic, except disintegrate, which destroys it at once. Blows, missiles, cold, heat, electricity and the like have no effect. Spells and breath weapons cannot pass through it in either direction. The caster can shape it into a hemisphere or sphere, with an area up to 20 square feet per level.

Component: a pinch of powdered diamond.

A vertical iron wall springs into being, one quarter of an inch thick per level of the caster, with an area of 15 square feet per level (180 square feet at 12th level). It is usually used to seal a passage or close a breach, since it fixes itself into any surrounding material if it is large enough. If created where it is not supported, it falls, crushing any creature beneath it. It is permanent unless dispelled, but is subject to everything a normal iron wall is (rust, perforation, etc.).

Component: a small piece of sheet iron.

Creates a wall of granite that merges with adjoining rock if the area allows, usually to close passages, portals and breaches against opponents. Per level of the caster it is ¼’ thick and 20 square feet in area: a 12th level magic-user makes a wall 3’ thick and 240 square feet (a 12’ wide and 20’ high wall, for example, to completely close a 10’ × 16’ passage).

Unlike a wall of iron, it need not be vertical or rest on a firm foundation, but it must merge with existing stone. It can bridge a chasm, for instance, or form a ramp. It is permanent unless destroyed by dispel magic or by normal means such as breaking, chipping, or a disintegrate spell.

Component: a small block of granite.

An invisible barrier surrounds the caster and moves with him or her. It is completely impervious to all magic and magical effects, including breath weapons, gaze weapons and voice weapons. No spells or their effects can enter, and no magic items or spells work inside it. Charmed, summoned and conjured creatures cannot enter. Normal creatures (a normal troll rather than a conjured one, for instance) and normal missiles can pass through. A magic sword would not work magically inside the shell, but it would still be a sword.

A stronger version of interposing hand (q.v.). Besides blocking, it pushes: it shoves away a creature weighing 500 pounds or less, slows a creature of 500 to 2,000 pounds to 1” per round, and slows a creature of up to 8,000 pounds by 50%. It takes as many hit points to destroy as its creator has.

Component: a glove.

Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the seventh level cleric spell control weather (q.v.). Components: burning incense, and bits of earth and wood mixed in water.

rolls.label: Delay before the weather is felt (turns, as the cleric spell)

system.description:
Instantly and irrevocably kills creatures in the area of effect. How many depends on their hit dice:

2 to 43-30 (3d10)

6 + 4 to 8 + 31-4 (1d4)

Mixed groups: use this conversion:

Equals Creatures with Hit Dice of:

4 + 1 to 6 + 383-.5

Roll the dice to see how many creatures of less than 2 hit dice are affected and kill them all, then use the conversion to kill the 2 to 4 hit dice monsters, and so on. If not enough of the number is left to kill the higher level ones, they survive. The order can be reversed, applying it to the highest hit dice victims first. Example: the 4d20 roll totals 53. 20 of this kills one 6 + 4 to 8 + 3 die creature (20 × .05 = 1); 16 kill two 4 + 1 to 6 + 3 hit dice creatures (16 × .125 = 2); 12 kill three 2 to 4 die creatures (3 × 4 = 12); and the remaining 5 kill 5 creatures of less than 2 dice (5 × 1 = 5); 20 + 16 + 12 + 5 = 53.

It does not affect lycanthropes, undead, or creatures not from the Prime Material Plane.

Component: a crushed black pearl worth at least 1,000 g.p.

Makes matter vanish, instantly and permanently. It works even on magical matter (or energy) such as forceful hand, but not on a globe of invulnerability or an anti-magic shell. Any living thing can be affected, even undead, and up to 1” cubic volume of non-living matter. Only 1 creature or object can be targeted. Creatures, and magical material that gets a saving throw, are unaffected if they save.

Components: a lodestone and a pinch of dust.

A magic-user planning to make a magic item must use this spell to prepare the object to receive its magic.

The item must: 1) be sound and undamaged; 2) be the finest possible of its kind, of the best materials and workmanship; and 3) have a cost or value that reflects this, in most cases a raw materials cost of over 100 g.p. Test 3) cannot apply to things like ropes, leather goods, cloth and pottery that are not normally embroidered, bejeweled, tooled, carved and/or engraved; but if such work or materials can be added without weakening or harming the item’s normal function, they are required.

Casting: the caster must touch the item constantly throughout the casting time, a base 16 hours plus 8-64 hours. Since a magic-user can never work more than 8 hours a day, and haste and other spells do not change the time, this means 2 days + 1-8 days. Work must be uninterrupted. During rest periods the item must never be more than 1’ from the caster, or the whole spell is spoiled and must be started over; and during rest no other magic of any kind may be done, and the caster must stay quiet and alone.

The final test: at the end the caster “knows” the item is ready and speaks the final magical syllable. The item then makes a saving throw versus magic, exactly as the caster’s (with the caster’s saving throw bonuses, up to but not over +3). A roll of 1 on the d20 always fails. If it succeeds, the caster can begin placing the desired dweomer on it, and must cast that spell within 24 hours or the preparation fades and the item must be enchanted again.

Adding spells: each spell then cast into the item takes 4 hours + 4-8 more hours per spell level. Again the caster must touch the item while casting and keep it within 1’ during rest. Each further dweomer must be begun within 24 hours of the last, even if an earlier one failed. The caster can tell whether enchant an item succeeded, but not whether later castings took, since each makes the same kind of saving throw the item did.

Permanence: no magic put on or into an item is permanent unless a permanency spell is used as the finishing touch, which always risks draining a point of constitution from the caster. Charged items (rods, staves, wands, javelins of lightning, ring of wishes, etc.) can never be made permanent. Scrolls and magic devices can never be used to enchant an item or to cast magic into a prepared one.

Components depend on the item and the magic to be placed in it. For example, a cloak of displacement might need the hides of 1 or more displacer beasts; a sword to slay dragons, the blood and some other part of the type(s) of dragon(s) it will work against; a ring of shooting stars, pieces of meteorites and the horn of a ki-rin. The Dungeon Master knows these specifics and other details of the spell.

rolls.label: Casting time beyond the base 16 hours (hours)

system.description: The same as the fourth level spell extension I, except that it doubles the duration of first through third level spells, and extends fourth or fifth level spells by 50% of their listed duration.

Places a magical command on a creature (usually human or humanoid) to perform some service, or to refrain from some action or course of activity, as the caster wishes. The creature must be intelligent, conscious and acting under its own will. A geas cannot force a creature to kill itself or do things likely to cause certain death, but can compel almost anything else.

The creature must follow the instructions until the geas is completed. If it fails to, it grows sick and dies within 1 to 4 weeks. Straying from or twisting the instructions costs it strength points until it stops. A wish removes a geas, but dispel magic and remove curse do not. The referee gives any further details: casting and fulfilling a geas is tricky, and an improperly cast geas is null and void at once (cf. wish).

Makes a section of metal, stone or wood as transparent as glass to the caster’s gaze, or actually turns it into transparent material. Normally up to four inches of metal, 6’ of stone, or 20’ of wood can be seen through. It does not work on lead, gold or platinum.

The caster can either make it work for himself or herself only, using it up to once per round while the spell lasts, or create an actual transparent area, a one-way window, in the material. Either way the viewing area is 3’ wide by 2’ high.

Component: a small piece of crystal or glass.

The same as the fourth level spell minor globe of invulnerability (q.v.), except for casting time, and it stops first through fourth level spells from affecting the magic-user inside. The caster can still cast spells out through it, of course.

A special and powerful spell mainly used to defend the magic-user’s stronghold. When cast, the following happen in the area of effect:

  1. All corridors fill with mist, cutting visibility to 10’.
  2. All doors are wizard locked.
  3. One door per level of the caster is covered by an illusion making it look like a plain wall.
  4. Stairs are filled with webs from top to bottom.
  5. Wherever there is a choice of direction (such as a cross or side passage), a minor confusion-type effect makes it 50% likely that intruders believe they are going the exact opposite way.
  6. The whole area radiates magic.
  7. The caster can add one of these: A. dancing lights in four corridors; B. magic mouths in two places; C. stinking clouds in two places; D. gust of wind in one corridor or room; or E. suggestion in one place.

Items 3 and 7 only work if the caster is totally familiar with the area. Each casting of dispel magic removes one effect, chosen at random. Remove curse does not work.

Components: burning incense, a small measure of sulphur and oil, a knotted string, a small amount of umber hulk blood and a small silver rod.

Summons an invisible stalker, an 8 hit die monster, from the Elemental Plane of Air. It obeys the caster and performs whatever tasks it is given, even hundreds or thousands of miles away. But it serves because it is bound to, not from loyalty or desire, so it resents long missions or complex tasks and will try to twist its instructions accordingly (for full details see 1e Fantasy RPG, MM).

Components: burning incense and a piece of horn carved into a crescent.

Finds out what information is available about a known person, place or thing. It reveals information only if the subject is noteworthy or legendary.

Casting time: 1 to 4 turns if the person or thing is at hand or the caster is in the place (and the chance of results is far greater); 1 to 10 days if detailed information is known; 2 to 12 weeks if only rumors are known. While casting, the magic-user can do nothing but routine things (eating, sleeping, etc.).

Results: the divination shows whether legendary material exists, and often where it is, by place name, rhyme or riddle. Sometimes (when the subject is at hand) it gives some information about the subject itself, but always in cryptic form (rhyme, riddle, anagram, cipher, sign, etc.).

Components: incense and strips of ivory formed into a rectangle, plus the sacrifice of some item: a potion, magic scroll, magic item, creature, etc.

The same as the fourth level cleric spell lower water (q.v.), except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics, that the reverse raises water only ½’ per level of the caster, and that the material components are a small vial of water and a small vial of dust.
Summons 1 to 3 fourth level monsters, arriving within 1 to 3 rounds. See monster summoning I for other details.

Moves dirt (clay, loam, sand) and the other things in it, so embankments can be collapsed, hillocks moved, dunes shifted, etc. Casting takes 1 turn for every 4” square of area. To move terrain features (rather than simply caving in banks or walls of earth), an earth elemental must be summoned afterwards to help. All casting and summoning must be finished before anything happens. Rock outcrops can never be collapsed or moved.

Components: a mix of soils (clay, loam, sand) in a small bag, and an iron blade.

A powerful spell with three uses; the component depends on which is chosen, and is lost on casting:

  • Freezing globe: a globe of matter at absolute zero that spreads over water, or liquid mostly made of water, freezing it to a depth of 6 inches over 100 square feet per level of the caster. The ice lasts 1 round per level. Component: a thin sheet of crystal about an inch square.
  • Ray of cold: a thin ray from the caster’s hand, reaching 1” per level, doing 4 hit points of damage per level to the creature struck. A successful saving throw versus magic negates all damage (the ray is so narrow that a save means it missed), but the ray continues its full distance, and anything else in its path must save (if applicable) or take damage. Component: a white sapphire worth at least 1,000 g.p.
  • Cold globe: a small globe about the size of a sling stone, cool to the touch but harmless. Thrown or slung, it shatters on impact, doing 4-24 hit points of cold damage to all creatures within a 10’ radius (one-half on a successful saving throw versus magic). If not thrown within 1 round per level of the caster, it shatters on its own with the same effect, which can be used against pursuers but can also endanger the caster and companions. Component: a diamond worth at least 1,000 g.p.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, and the material components (two small sheets of crystal or glass), this is the same as the sixth level cleric spell part water (q.v.).

Creates a non-material duplicate of the caster at any spot within range. The image copies whatever the caster chooses to do: walking, speaking, casting spells. A special channel links image and caster, so spells the caster casts actually come from the image. Attacks do not affect it; only dispel magic (or the caster’s command) ends it. The caster must keep the image in view at all times; if his or her sight of it is blocked, the spell ends.

Component: a small replica (doll) of the caster.

Similar to the seventh level druid spell reincarnate (q.v.). No saving throw for system shock or resurrection survival is needed. The corpse is touched, and a new incarnation appears in the area in 1 to 6 turns, if the person has been dead no longer than 1 day per level of the caster. The new incarnation is:

Very good or very evil persons are not reincarnated as creatures of generally opposite alignment.

Components: a small drum and a drop of blood.

All creatures in the area of effect are pushed away from the caster, at 3” per round or at the speed the creature is using to try to approach, and keep moving away for the rest of a complete move even if this takes them beyond range.

Component: a pair of small magnetized iron bars attached to two small dog statuettes, one ivory and one ebony.

A very strong protection/punishment spell against the powerful creatures of the nether planes (Abyssal, Hades, Hell, etc.). The caster must know the name of the being it is aimed at.

Preparation: the caster must personally make an illuminated sheet of vellum, carefully inscribed with the being’s name in special inks made from powdered rubies and the ichor of a slain type I, II or III demon, with a continuous border of gold leaf. This takes 8-32 hours and costs 1,000 g.p. for the vellum, special pens, gold leaf and other materials, plus at least 5,000 g.p. of powdered rubies per document. The demon, devil or other powerful nether being must then be present in some form (not possessing another creature’s body) for the caster to begin.

Reading the document takes three rounds:

  1. As soon as reading begins, the named being is rooted to the spot unless it makes its magic resistance percentage (adjusted for the caster’s level) as a saving throw. Even if it saves, it feels very uncomfortable, and unless it has been magically forced there and held, it is 90% likely to flee to its own (or another) plane, since it is powerless to attack the caster while the document is being read. Its discomfort grows through this first round.
  2. During the second minute, the being suffers acute pain and loses 1 hit point per hit die. By the end of the round it is in wracking pain.
  3. The third and final round costs it 50% of its remaining hit points, causes horrible pain, and at the end banishes it to some confined space on its own plane, there to stay in torment for as many years as the level of the caster who prepared the document.

A being treated this way becomes the caster’s sworn enemy forever, so a magic-user will be reluctant to finish the spell and will rather use it as a threat to force the being to submit. Each round of reading it is forced to hear makes the being a cumulative 25% likely to give in, even without any other offering or payment.

Turns any kind of stone into flesh. If the stone was once a living creature, of any size, it is restored to life (along with its possessions), though it must make the usual system shock survival roll. Ordinary stone can also be turned to flesh, 9 cubic feet per level of the caster.

Reverse: turns flesh of any kind to stone in the same way, along with everything the creature carries. The intended victim gets a saving throw.

Components: a pinch of earth and a drop of blood; lime, water and earth for the reverse.

The caster swells to heroic size and strength and becomes a berserk fighter, an astonishing sight to anyone not expecting it:

  • Hit points double. Damage is taken from the extra magical points first, so damage that does not exceed the added amount does no real harm; but each point of damage beyond the extra amount counts as 2 (double damage).
  • Armor class improves by a full 4 places (AC 10 becomes 6, AC 9 becomes 5, AC 8 becomes 4, etc.).
  • Attacks are made as a fighter of the caster’s level (using the fighters’ combat table).
  • The caster can only attack with a dagger, but does +2 extra damage with it and makes 2 attacks per round.

The spell must run its full course: the caster keeps attacking until all opponents are dead, he or she is killed, the magic is dispelled, or the duration ends.

Component: a potion of heroism (or superheroism), drunk while casting.

A superior version of the sixth level spell forceful hand (q.v.), similar to it in many ways. The grasping hand can hold a creature or object of up to 1,000 pounds motionless, or move creatures as a forceful hand of double strength.

Component: a leather glove.

A dangerous spell that summons a powerful demon of type IV, V or VI whose name the caster knows. It is not strong enough to call a greater demon, and lesser kinds have no known names, so they are not called. The demon arrives very angry and evilly disposed. To avoid being slain or carried off, the caster must be inside a circle of protection (or a thaumaturgic triangle with protection from evil), and the demon must be confined in a pentagram (circled pentacle).

The summoned demon can be dealt with in three ways:

1) Force: by threat and pain of a spiritwrack spell (q.v.), the caster makes it perform a service and pledge its word to do so, freeing it when the service is fully done. This is extremely dangerous: the demon will seize on any small error in the bargain to reverse the intended result or simply kill and devour the summoner, and it hates the caster forever afterwards, so the caster had better be very powerful and capable.

2) Bargain: with a tribute of fresh human blood and the promise of 1 or more human sacrifices, the caster can bargain for willing service. Again the caster needs ample protection and power, since the demon may decide the offer is too small, or that the summoner’s slow death would be more enjoyable, and refuse. Because its name is known, the demon must keep its pledge, but only to the exact words of the deal, not its spirit. Only highly evil magic-users are likely to try this, and the demon may be favorably disposed toward such a character, especially a chaotic one.

3) Trap: the demon can be the target of a trap the soul spell (q.v.). The caster does not talk or bargain with it, though the demon may be eager to reach a deal before it is imprisoned. This is risky only without proper precautions, since failing to confine it usually just lets it escape to its own plane. Once trapped, it stays imprisoned until whoever holds its prison breaks it and frees it. It then owes one service; if the liberator(s) fail to demand one when it asks what is required, it is free to kill them on the spot, but if a service is demanded, it must first do its best to perform it and then return to the Abyss.

Limits on service: service must be limited in time unless the demon is willing to serve longer. A service that would take an unreasonable time, or is impossible, is 50% likely to free the demon from its obligations and leave it free to take revenge on the caster if he or she is not continually protected afterwards, since a demon freed this way can stay on the plane it was summoned to for as long as 666 days.

The demon is exceptionally strong: 8 hit points per hit die.

Casting time: 1 hour per type number of the demon. Any interruption during casting makes the spell fail. Any interruption while the demon is present gives it a 10% chance to break out of its bounds and attack the caster, rising cumulatively each round the interruption continues.

Saving throw: each demon gets a saving throw against the summoning: if it rolls higher than the caster’s level on 3d6 (2d10 for type VI demons), the spell fails to bring it. When that happens, the named demon is certainly imprisoned or destroyed, or the name was not perfectly correct, so the caster must call another name.

Components: 5 flaming black candles; a brazier of hot coals on which are burned sulphur, bat hairs, lard, soot, mercuric-nitric acid crystals, mandrake root, alcohol, and a piece of parchment with the demon’s name written in runes inside a pentacle; and a dish of blood from some mammal (preferably a human, of course) placed where the demon is to be held.

rolls.label: Summoning check (fails if higher than the caster's level)

system.description:
Brings plants in a 3” × 1” area under the caster’s command. The caster can communicate with them, and they obey as well as they can. The spell gives them no new abilities, but they use whatever they have to carry out instructions, including any special or unusual abilities. Only intelligent plants get a saving throw, made at -4.

Components: a pinch of humus, a drop of water and a twig or leaf.

Creates a fireball with +1 on each die of damage, which does not explode for 1 to 50 segments (1/10 to 5 rounds), as the caster commands when casting. Otherwise it is the same as the third level spell fireball (q.v.).

Teleports a chosen item from virtually anywhere straight into the caster’s hand. It must be a single, non-living object no longer than a sword and no heavier than a shield (about 75 g.p. weight).

Preparation: holding a gem worth at least 5,000 g.p., the caster touches the item, names it specifically, and speaks all but the last word of the spell. Later, the caster speaks the final word while crushing that same gem, and the item appears instantly in whichever hand the caster wants. Only that particular item can be summoned.

Limits: if another creature has the item, the spell fails, but the caster learns who has it and roughly where. Items can be summoned from other planes, but only if no other creature possesses them (not necessarily holding them). At 14th level the item can be 1 plane away from the caster’s plane, at 15th 2, at 16th 3, etc. So a 16th level magic-user could summon an item from the second layer of one of the outer planes, while at 14th level the item would have to be on one of the Elemental Planes or the Astral or Ethereal Plane.

The caster has only two dimensions: height and width but no depth. Turned sideways, he or she is invisible, detectable only by true seeing or similar means. The caster can slip through the thinnest gap that is tall enough (going between a door and its frame is easy), and can act normally: turn invisible, move, appear the next round and cast a spell, vanish again the following round, and so on.

While turned, the caster cannot be affected by any attack. While visible, he or she takes triple normal damage from any attack: a dagger thrust that hits would do 3-12 hit points.

Part of the caster exists on the Astral Plane during the spell, and may be noticed by creatures there. If noticed, there is a 25% chance that an astral creature’s attack pulls the caster entirely onto the Astral Plane.

Components: a thin, flat ivory likeness of the caster (of the finest workmanship, gold filigreed, enameled and gem-studded, costing 5,000 to 10,000 g.p. on average) and a strip of parchment. As the spell is spoken, the parchment is given a half twist and its ends joined; the figurine is passed through the loop, and both vanish forever.

A very potent but difficult spell. It grants the caster’s words literally, but only partly or for a limited time. It can alter what is real in the past, present or future in some limited way (possibly only for the caster, unless the wish is worded very carefully). It will not substantially change major realities, nor bring wealth or experience just for the asking.

For example, it can restore some lost hit points (or all of them for a limited time), reduce opponents’ chances to hit or their damage, extend some magical effect, make a creature friendly to the caster, and so on (cf. wish). It might give a minor clue to some treasure or magic item. Greedy wishes usually end in disaster for the wisher. Casting time is the actual number of seconds (six per segment) taken to phrase the wish.
The same as invisibility (q.v.), but it hides creatures in a 3” × 3” area: up to 300 to 400 man-sized creatures, 30 to 40 giants, or 6 to 8 large dragons.
Summons 1-2 fifth level monsters, arriving in 1-3 rounds. See monster summoning I for other details.

Creates a shimmering, sword-shaped plane of force that the caster wields mentally, moving and striking with it as a fighter would. While doing so the caster can do nothing else but move.

  • To hit: as a sword wielded by a fighter of one-half the caster’s level (a 14th level magic-user’s sword hits as a 7th level fighter’s). It has no magical bonus “to hit”, but can hit any opponent, even those normally hit only by +3 weapons, and astral, ethereal or out of phase ones, and it hits any armor class on a roll of 19 or 20.
  • Damage: 5-20 hit points against man-size or smaller opponents, 5-30 against larger. It can be used to subdue.

It lasts until the duration ends, dispel magic succeeds against it, or the caster no longer wants it.

Component: a miniature platinum sword with a grip and pommel of copper and zinc, costing 500 g.p. to make, which vanishes after the spell.

The caster attunes his or her body to a section of wall, which is affected as if by passwall (q.v.). The phase door is invisible to everyone but the caster, and only the caster can use it, disappearing on entering and reappearing on leaving. It lasts for 1 use per 2 levels of the caster. It can only be dispelled by a higher level magic-user casting dispel magic, or by several lower level magic-users casting together whose combined levels are more than double the caster’s.

When the word is spoken, one creature of the caster’s choice, which the caster must be facing and which must be within range (½” per level), is stunned: reeling and unable to think straight or act. How long depends on its current hit points (use its present total if it is below its usual maximum):

Hit pointsStunned for
1 to 304-16 (4d4) rounds
31 to 602 to 8 (2d4) rounds
61 to 901 to 4 (d4) rounds
over 90not affected

Reverses gravity in the area, so all unfixed objects and creatures in it “fall” upward. It lasts 1 second (1/6 segment), during which they “fall” 16’ up. Anything that hits a solid object in this “fall” strikes it just as in a normal downward fall. When the spell ends, everything affected falls back down. Since it affects an area, objects tens, hundreds or even thousands of feet up can be affected.

Components: a lodestone and iron filings.

Creates a duplicate of any creature that looks exactly like the real one, formed from ice or snow. The spell is cast over the rough form, with some piece of the creature to be copied placed inside the snow or ice, and powdered ruby is also required.

Differences from the original: it has only 51% to 60% (50% + 1% to 10%) of the original’s hit points; its personality differs; it lacks some areas of knowledge; and detect magic or true seeing instantly reveals it. On its own the spell makes only a zombie-like form. A reincarnation spell must be used to give it vital force, and a limited wish to give it 40% to 65% (35% + 5% to 30%) of the original’s knowledge and personality. Its level, if any, is 20% to 50% of the original’s. It can never become more powerful (it cannot gain levels or abilities).

The simulacrum is always under the absolute command of its maker, but there is no special telepathic link, so orders must be given in the normal way.

The caster or another creature, with everything worn or carried, apparently turns to solid stone. The change takes 1 full round after casting. Afterwards the subject passes any inspection as a stone statue, though a faint magic can be detected if checked for. The subject still sees, hears and smells normally, but feels only what would actually affect its granite-hard body: chipping is like a slight wound, but breaking off an arm is another matter.

While the spell lasts, the subject can return to normal in 1/6 of a segment, and back to stone just as fast, as often as desired.

Survival: during the first change from flesh to stone, the subject must roll 82% or less on percentile dice, subtracting 1 from the roll for each point of constitution (so 18 constitution means certain success). Failure means system shock and death.

Components: lime, sand and a drop of water, stirred with an iron bar such as a nail or spike.

Makes an object vanish. Both weight and volume limit the spell: at most 3 cubic feet per level of the caster.

  • An object weighing up to 500 g.p. per level of the caster (7,000 g.p. at 14th level) is teleported (see teleport) to wherever the caster wants.
  • A heavier object is instead placed on the ethereal plane and replaced with stone. A door made to vanish is replaced by a stone wall 1’ thick, or as thick as the door, whichever is greater.

A successful dispel magic brings vanished items back from the ethereal plane.

Sets up vibrations that either repel or attract one specific kind of living, intelligent creature, or characters of one particular alignment. The caster must choose the effect, and the creature or alignment, before casting, since the components differ. The kind of creature must be named specifically (red dragons, hill giants, wererats, lammasu, catoblepas, vampires, etc.), as must an alignment (chaotic evil, chaotic good, lawful neutral, neutral, etc.). It cannot be cast on living creatures.

Antipathy: the chosen creatures feel an overpowering urge to leave the area or not touch the item. On a failed saving throw versus magic, they must leave it and shun it permanently, never willingly entering or touching it until the spell is removed or ends. On a successful save they may stay or touch it, but feel very uncomfortable, and a persistent itching costs them 1 point of dexterity per round they stay or touch, to a maximum of 4 points. Component: a lump of alum soaked in vinegar.

Sympathy: the chosen creatures feel elated and pleased to be in the area, or at the thought of touching or owning the item, with an overpowering desire to stay or to keep it. Unless they save versus magic, they stay or refuse to let go. A creature that saves is released, but must save again 1-6 turns later, and if that save fails it returns to the area or object. Components: 1,000 g.p. worth of crushed pearls and a drop of honey.

Area: cast on an area, it covers a 10’ cube per level of the caster. Cast on an object, only that single thing is enchanted, but affected creatures save against it at -2.

Creates a huge disembodied hand clenched into a fist, which the caster controls mentally and can make strike an opponent each round. The caster can do no other spell casting or magical activity while the spell lasts. The fist never misses, but the force of its blow varies; roll d20 each round:

d20Result
1-12glancing blow: 1 to 6 hit points
13-16solid punch: 2 to 12 hit points
17-19hard punch: 3 to 18 hit points, and the opponent is stunned next round
20crushing blow: 4 to 24 hit points, and the opponent is stunned for the next 3 rounds

Against a stunned opponent the caster adds +4 to the roll, since it cannot dodge or defend itself well. (This spell can be used with any of the other hand spells.) The fist is destroyed when it has taken damage equal to the caster’s hit points.

Components: a leather glove, and a small device of four rings joined to form a slightly curved line, with an “I” on which the bottoms of the rings rest, all made of an alloy of copper and zinc.

rows.text: hard punch, opponent stunned next round
crushing blow, opponent stunned for the next 3 rounds

system.description:
Creates a duplicate of a person, identical in every way, including level of experience, memories, etc. Grown from a small piece of the person’s flesh (the material component), the clone takes 2-8 months to grow. It is the person as he or she was when the flesh was taken, and knows nothing of anything learned or experienced afterwards. It is a physical duplicate only; the original’s possessions are another matter entirely.

Two of the same: because the duplicate really is the person, once both exist each knows of the other, and each wants to destroy the other, since such an alter ego is unbearable to both. If one cannot destroy the other within 1 week of the dual existence beginning, then either (95%) one goes insane and destroys itself (75% likely to be the clone), or (5%) both go mad and commit suicide.

Turns crystal or glass into a transparent substance with the tensile strength and unbreakability of real steel. Only a fairly small amount can be affected, up to 10 pounds per level of the caster, and it must be one whole object.

Components: a small piece of glass and a small piece of steel.

Exactly like the smoke effect of pyrotechnics (q.v.), except that the cloud is at least 10’ high by 20’ long and wide. The dense cloud billows out and then begins to burn:

  • 3rd round: ½ hit point of damage per level of the caster.
  • 4th round: 1 hit point per level.
  • 5th round: ½ hit point per level again as the flames die out.
  • Any later rounds: harmless smoke that blocks vision inside it.

A creature inside makes a saving throw to take one-half damage. If its first save succeeds, it needs no more; if it fails, it rolls again on the 4th and 5th rounds (if needed).

Components: a fire source (as for pyrotechnics), scrapings from beneath a dung pile and a pinch of dust.

Works like charm person or charm monster (qq.v.), on either persons or monsters, but affects any number of creatures whose combined levels and/or hit dice do not exceed twice the caster’s level. All must be within range and within an area of at most 3” by 3”. The number of targets does not change the saving throws (cf. charm person and charm monster), but all targets save at -2 because of the spell’s power.

Sends the target into an extra-dimensional space, a shifting labyrinth of force planes, where it wanders for a time that depends entirely on its intelligence. Minotaurs are not affected.

Intelligence of
Mazed CreatureTime Trapped In Maze
under 32 to 8 turns
3 to 51 to 4 turns
6 to 85 to 20 rounds
9 to 114 to 16 rounds
12 to 143 to 12 rounds
15 to 172 to 8 rounds
18 and up1 to 4 rounds

The recipient is completely protected from all devices and/or spells that detect, influence or read emotions and/or thoughts. This includes augury, charm, command, confusion, divination, empathy (all forms), ESP, fear, feeblemind, mass suggestion, phantasmal killer, possession, rulership, soul trapping, suggestion and telepathy. It also prevents discovery or information gathering by crystal balls or other scrying devices, clairaudience, clairvoyance, communing, contacting other planes, or wish-related methods (wishing, limited wish, alter reality). Exceedingly powerful deities could still get through.

It also protects against psionic detection and/or influence, such as domination (or mass domination), hypnosis, invisibility (the psionic kind works on the mind) and precognition, as well as the powers already covered as spells.
Summons 1 or 2 sixth level monsters, arriving in 1 to 3 rounds. See monster summoning I for other details.

The target starts dancing, feet shuffling and tapping, and can do nothing but caper and prance. Its armor class worsens by 4, it cannot make saving throws, and its shield counts for nothing. The creature must be touched, possibly requiring a roll as if the caster were striking it in melee.

Makes the duration of certain other spells permanent. The magic-user casts the spell first, then permanency. Each permanency spell costs the magic-user 1 point of constitution.

On the caster himself or herself (not on other creatures), these spells can be made permanent:

comprehend languagesprotection from evil
detect evilprotection from normal missiles
detect invisibilityread magic
detect magictongues
infravisionunseen servant

This use can only be dispelled by a magic-user of higher level than the caster was when casting it.

On objects, creatures or areas, these spells can be made lasting:

enlargeprismatic sphere
fearstinking cloud
gust of windwall of fire
invisibilitywall of force
magic mouthweb

For these, permanency can be cast at the same time as the other spell when no living creature is the target, but it can be dispelled normally, which negates the whole spell.

Changes one object, living or not, into another. Used like polymorph other or stone to flesh, it is simply a stronger version, with saving throws at -4. Used to change other things, its duration depends on how different the new form is from the original, and on the difference in size. The Dungeon Master decides this by comparing:

  • kingdom: animal, vegetable, mineral
  • class: mammals, bipeds, fungi, metals, spheres, etc.
  • relationship: twig is to tree, sand is to beach, etc.
  • size: smaller, equal, larger
  • shape: how much the original resembles the new form
  • intelligence: especially where the new form is more intelligent

A change of kingdom makes the spell last hours or turns: hours if one kingdom removed, turns if two removed. Other differences shorten it too. Turning a lion into an androsphinx would be permanent, but a turnip into a purple worm would last only hours; a tusk into an elephant would be permanent, but a twig into a sword only several turns.

All polymorphed objects radiate strong magic, and dispel magic returns them to their natural form. Stone to flesh, or its reverse, affects objects under this spell. System shock applies to living creatures, as do the limits given for polymorph other and stone to flesh (qq.v.).

Components: mercury, gum arabic and smoke.

Makes one or more creatures in range and area of effect temporarily blind. It affects up to 100 hit points of creatures; creatures with over 100 hit points are not affected. Before rolling, the caster must say which creatures are targeted, naming one as the center. Duration depends on the total hit points affected: 50 or less, 2 to 5 (d4 + 1) turns; 51 or more, only 2 to 5 rounds. Cure blindness or dispel magic removes the blindness.

The magic-user gives those he or she touches near immunity to certain spells and magical attacks. One creature can be protected per 4 levels of the caster, but the duration is divided among them: a 16th level magic-user can protect 1 creature for 16 turns, 2 creatures for 8 turns, or 4 creatures for 4 turns. The protection gives these saving throw bonuses:

AgainstSaving throw bonus
Beguiling, Charm, Suggestion+9
Command, Domination, Fear, Hold, Scare+7
Geas, Quest+5

Components: a diamond, crushed and sprinkled over the recipients, and each recipient must also carry an intact diamond of any size.

Creates magical runes that affect creatures who pass over, touch or read them, or pass through a portal they are written on. The caster writes the symbol on any surface, choosing one of these:

  • Death: one or more creatures with a total of no more than 80 hit points are slain.
  • Discord: all creatures immediately start bickering and arguing loudly, with a 50% chance that creatures of different alignment attack each other. Bickering lasts 5-20 rounds, fighting 2-8 rounds.
  • Fear: an extra-strong fear spell; all creatures must save at -4 or panic and flee as if affected by fear.
  • Hopelessness: all creatures must save versus magic or turn back in dejection. Affected creatures give in to any opponent’s demands (surrender, get out, etc.). Lasts 3 to 12 (3d4) turns; during it, each round there is a 25% chance an affected creature does nothing, and 25% that one that does act turns back or withdraws from battle, as applicable.
  • Insanity: one or more creatures with a total of no more than 120 hit points go insane and act as if under a confusion spell (q.v.) until heal, restoration or wish cures the madness.
  • Pain: all creatures suffer wracking pains: -2 dexterity and -4 on attack rolls for 2-20 turns.
  • Sleep: all creatures under 8 + 1 hit dice fall into a catatonic slumber and cannot be woken for 5 to 16 (d12 + 4) turns.
  • Stunning: one or more creatures with a total of no more than 160 hit points are stunned and reeling for 3-12 (3d4) rounds, dropping anything held.

The kind of symbol cannot be identified without reading it, which sets it off.

Components: powdered black opal and diamond dust, each worth at least 5,000 g.p.

Like magic jar, but it forces the target’s life force (and its material body, if any) into a special prison prepared by the caster. The caster must see the target and know its true name when speaking the final word.

The prison: a gem worth 1,000 g.p. per hit die or level of the creature (10,000 g.p. for a 10 hit dice or 10th level creature). The caster prepares it with enchant an item and then places a maze spell into it.

Two ways to trap the soul:

  • Speak the final word with the creature in range. It gets its magic resistance (if any) and also a saving throw versus magic; if it saves, the gem shatters.
  • Far more insidious: trick the victim into accepting a trigger object inscribed with the final word, which traps its soul automatically as soon as it picks up or accepts the item. The trigger item must be named when the gem is prepared, and a sympathy spell may be placed on it.

The gem holds the soul indefinitely, until broken; the soul is then released and its body re-forms. If the trapped creature is a powerful being from another plane (which could include a character trapped by an inhabitant of another plane while not on the Prime Material Plane), it can be required to perform a service as soon as it is freed. Otherwise the creature goes completely free when the gem is broken.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the seventh level cleric spell astral spell (q.v.).

Creates a huge disembodied hand, like forceful hand and clenched fist (qq.v.), which the caster controls mentally to grasp and squeeze an opponent. The damage grows with each round it keeps squeezing:

RoundDamage
1st round1-10 hit points
2nd & 3rd rounds2-20 hit points
4th & beyond4-40 hit points

The hand is dispelled after taking damage equal to its creator’s hit points.

Components: a snake skin glove and an eggshell.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the seventh level cleric spell gate (q.v.).

The creature touched is entombed in suspended animation (cf. temporal stasis) in a small sphere far below the surface of the earth, and stays there unless the reverse of the spell is cast with the creature’s name and background. The spell only works if the victim’s name and background are known. Magical searches by crystal ball, locate object or similar means will not reveal that the creature is imprisoned.

Reverse (freedom): the victim reappears at the spot where it was entombed and sunk into the earth. If the caster does not get the creature’s name and background exactly right, there is a 10% chance that 1 to 100 other imprisoned creatures are freed at the same time.

rolls.label: Others freed by a flawed freedom (10% chance)

system.description:
A very powerful, spectacular spell, similar in many ways to fireball. Either four spheres 2’ across or eight spheres 1’ across spring from the caster’s outstretched hand and streak in a straight line as far as the caster chooses, up to maximum range, leaving a fiery trail of sparks. Each then bursts like a fireball (q.v.). Any creature in the straight path of a missile takes its full effect with no saving throw.

  • Four large spheres: each does 10 to 40 hit points of damage in a 3” diameter area. They burst in a diamond or box pattern, each 2” apart along the sides, so their areas overlap and the center is caught by all four blasts.
  • Eight small spheres: each has half the diameter (1½”) and half the damage (5-20). They burst in a box within a diamond, or the reverse, with outer sides 2” long and inner sides 1” long. The center is caught by 4 overlapping areas, and many areas around the edge by two.

Creatures in each area make a separate saving throw for each burst, taking full or half damage, except those directly hit by a missile as noted above.
Summons 1 or 2 seventh level monsters, arriving 1 round after casting, or 1 8th level monster, arriving after 2 rounds. See monster summoning I for other details.

Slays creatures in range and area of effect: either one creature with up to 60 hit points, or 2 or more creatures with 10 or fewer hit points each, up to 120 hit points in total. The caster must state whether one or several creatures are targeted, along with the range and center of the area.

Surrounds the caster with an opaque globe of shimmering, multi-colored layers of light that protects against all forms of attack. It flashes all seven colors of the visible spectrum, each layer with its own power. Any creature with fewer than eight hit dice is blinded by the colors for 2 to 8 turns. The sphere cannot move, and only the caster can pass in and out without harm. Since the caster is at its center, usually only the upper half shows; the lower half is hidden by the floor.

ColorOrderEffect of layerNegated by
red1ststops all non-magical missiles; inflicts 10 hit points of damagecone of cold
orange2ndstops all magical missiles; inflicts 20 hit points of damagegust of wind
yellow3rdstops poisons, gasses and petrification; inflicts 40 hit points of damagedisintegrate
green4thstops all breath weapons; save vs. poison or deadpasswall
blue5thstops location/detection and psionics; save vs. petrification or turned to stonemagic missile
indigo6thstops all magical spells; save vs. wand or insanecontinual light
violet7thforce field protection; save vs. magic or sent to another planedispel magic

A rod of cancellation destroys a prismatic sphere. Otherwise anything entering it is destroyed, and a creature suffers the effect of every layer: 70 hit points of damage plus death, petrification, insanity and/or instant transport to another plane; only those last four allow saving throws. The layers can be destroyed by the right magical attacks, but only in order: the 1st before any others, then the 2nd, etc.

The caster can take the form of any creature short of a demi-god, greater devil, demon prince, unique dragon type, greater demon or the like. He or she becomes that creature, with all its abilities except those that depend on intelligence, since the mind stays the caster’s. Each new form has the hit points the caster has at the time of the change. Each change takes 1 segment, and there is no system shock. The caster can change from a griffon to an efreet to a titan, etc.

Example: a wizard in combat becomes a will o’ wisp; when that form stops being useful, the wizard becomes a stone golem and walks away; pursued, the golem becomes a flea hiding on a horse until it can hop off and become a bush; if detected as the bush, the wizard can become a dragon, a pool of water, or almost anything else.

Component: a jade circlet worth at least 5,000 g.p., which shatters when the spell ends. Meanwhile it is left behind at the first change, and if it is shattered early, the magic ends.

Places the creature in suspended animation. Time stops for it: it does not age, and its body functions virtually cease. This lasts until removed by dispel magic or the reverse spell (temporal reinstatement), which needs only a single word and no somatic or material components.

Component: a powder of diamond, emerald, ruby and sapphire dust, one stone of each kind.

Time stops in the area of effect; from outside, the sphere seems to shimmer for an instant. For the spell’s duration (which is subjective to the caster), the caster can move and act freely in the area, while every other creature there is frozen between ticks of the clock. Any creature entering the area is also stopped in time, and if the caster leaves it, the spell ends at once. When the spell ends, the caster is back in normal time.

A more potent version of limited wish (q.v.). Using it to change reality regarding hit points the party has lost, to bring a dead character back to life, or to escape a difficult situation by moving the caster (and his or her party) from one place to another causes the caster no disability. Any other kind of wish leaves the caster weak (-3 strength) and needing 2 to 8 days of bed rest, because of the strain it puts on time, space and the caster’s body.

Whatever is wished for, the exact wording of the wish is likely to be carried out. (The referee needs this discretion to keep the game balanced. Wishing another character dead would be grossly unfair, for example, so the DM might send the wisher to a future time when the target is no longer alive, putting the wishing character out of the campaign.)

rolls.label: Bed rest after a strenuous wish (days)

system.description: Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the second level magic-user spell audible glamer (q.v.).

The illusionist changes how he or she looks, including clothing and equipment: up to 1’ shorter or taller; thin, fat or in between; human, humanoid or any other generally man-shaped two-legged creature. Lasts 2 to 12 (2d6) rounds plus 2 rounds per level of the caster.

A vivid fan-shaped spray of clashing colors bursts from the illusionist’s hand, affecting 1 to 6 creatures in the area, up to a total of 1 level or hit die per level of the caster. The effect depends on each creature’s level or hit dice compared with the caster’s:

  • Equal to or less than the caster’s: unconscious for 2 to 8 rounds.
  • 1 or 2 greater: blinded for 1 to 4 rounds.
  • 3 or more greater: stunned (cf. power word, stun, seventh level magic-user spell) for 2 to 8 segments.

All creatures of higher level than the caster, and all creatures of 6th level or 6 hit dice, get a saving throw.

Components: a pinch each of red, yellow and blue colored powder or sand.
The same as the first level magic-user spell dancing lights (q.v.).
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the second level magic-user spell darkness (q.v.).

The illusionist can see an illusion and know it for exactly that. The caster can also let another creature see illusions as unreal by touching it with both hands while it looks at the illusion.

Component: a piece of yellow tinted crystal, glass or mica.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the second level magic-user spell detect invisibility (q.v.).
Creates a mirror-like area of air in front of the illusionist. Any gaze attack, such as a basilisk’s or a medusa’s, is reflected back on the gazer if it looks at the caster.

The illusionist’s gestures and droning chant make 1 to 6 creatures susceptible to suggestion (see the third level magic-user spell suggestion). The suggestion is given after the hypnotism is cast, and until then the caster does not know whether the spell worked. The suggestion itself is not a spell, just a spoken urging. Creatures that make their saving throw are not hypnotized.
The same as the first level magic-user spell light (q.v.) (cf. the first level cleric spell light).
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the third level magic-user spell phantasmal force (q.v.).

Creates a wall of misty vapor anywhere the illusionist wants within range. It blocks all sight, normal and/or infravision, beyond 2’. Its size is a cube 2” on a side per level of the caster. It lasts 3 or more rounds unless blown away by a strong breeze (cf. gust of wind).

Component: a pinch of split dried peas.
The target goes blind, seeing only grayness. Cure spells do not remove this; if the target fails its initial saving throw, only dispel magic or the caster can end the blindness.

The illusionist’s outline becomes blurred, shifting and wavering. All missile and melee attacks against the caster are at -4 on the first attempt and -2 on all later ones, and the caster gets +1 on saving throws against any direct magical attack.

The target becomes totally deaf (cf. blindness). The victim gets a saving throw. Only dispel magic or the caster can end the deafness.

Component: beeswax.
Similar to the first level cleric and first level magic-user spells detect magic (qq.v.).

A billowing mass of misty greenish vapor that looks like a cloudkill (q.v.). It moves away from the caster at 1” per round and behaves in most ways like a cloudkill, but its only effect is to block vision, as a wall of fog does.

Creates a weaving, turning pattern of subtle colors in the air. Any creature that looks at it becomes fascinated and stands gazing as long as the illusionist keeps the glowing lines moving. It can captivate up to 24 levels or hit dice of creatures (24 creatures of 1 hit die, 12 of 2 hit dice, etc.), all within the area of effect, and each gets a saving throw.

The caster need not make a sound, but must gesture while holding a glowing stick of incense or a crystal rod filled with phosphorescent material.

The same as the third level magic-user spell phantasmal force (q.v.), except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics and these: the caster can keep up the illusion with minimal concentration, moving at half normal speed (but not casting other spells); the illusion includes some minor sounds, but no understandable speech; and by concentrating on the form of the phantasm, the caster makes it last 2 rounds after concentration stops.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the second level magic-user spell invisibility (q.v.).
The same as the second level magic-user spell magic mouth (q.v.).
The same as the second level magic-user spell mirror image (q.v.), except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics, and that it creates 2-5 (d4 + 1) images.

Misdirects the information from a detection spell: detect charm, detect evil, detect invisibility, detect lie, detect magic, or detect snares & pits. The illusionist casts it on the creature or item that is the object of the detection. If the caster of the detection spell fails his or her saving throw, the detection still works but points to the wrong area or creature, or, for detect evil or detect lie, gives the opposite of the truth.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the first level magic-user spell ventriloquism (q.v.).
Creates a globe of impenetrable darkness. Its effects and material component are the same as the second level magic-user spell darkness, 15’ radius (cf. continual light).
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the cleric spell continual light (q.v.).

Dispels any phantasmal force (with or without audible glamer) cast by a non-illusionist. Against another illusionist’s illusion/phantasm spells it has the same chance as dispel magic (q.v.): 50% base, minus 2% per level the caster is below, or plus 5% per level above, the illusionist who cast the spell being dispelled.

system.aoe: 6” long cone, 3” diameter at end, ½” at base
system.description: Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the fourth level magic-user spell fear (q.v.).
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the fourth level magic-user spell hallucinatory terrain (q.v.).

The illusionist writes instructions or other information on parchment, paper, skin, etc., which looks like some foreign or magical writing. Only the person (or class of persons, etc.) the illusionist chooses can read it, though another illusionist will recognize it as illusionary script. Anyone else who tries to read it is confused, as by a confusion spell (q.v.), for 5 to 20 turns, minus 1 turn per level of the reader.

Component: a lead-based ink, specially made by an alchemist.

Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the third level magic-user spell invisibility, 10’ radius (q.v.). See also the second level magic-user spell invisibility.

Hides the illusionist from divination spells such as clairaudience, clairvoyance, “detects” and ESP, and from location by magic items such as crystal balls and medallions of ESP.

Component: a pinch of diamond dust.

Creates an illusion of muscle slowdown in creatures whose combined hit dice do not exceed twice the illusionist’s level. Those that fail their saving throws are paralyzed until dispel illusion or dispel magic is used, or until the illusionist chooses to end it.
The same as the second level magic-user spell rope trick (q.v.).
Creates an illusion that includes sound, smell and heat. Otherwise it is like the second level spell improved phantasmal force (q.v.). It lasts 3 rounds after the caster stops concentrating.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the third level magic-user spell suggestion (q.v.).
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the fourth level magic-user spell confusion (q.v.). See also the seventh level druid spell confusion.

The illusionist restores 50% of lost hit points to all persons (humans, demi-humans and humanoids) touched during the round of casting, up to four persons. The recipients are given the illusion that they are fresh and well, and their stamina is renewed, but when the spell ends they drop back to their actual hit points. While it lasts, recipients can move at double speed for 1 round in every turn (cf. haste).

The illusionist projects one of these 4 emotions, for as long as he or she keeps concentrating:

  1. Fear: the same as the spell of that name, but since it is not an illusion, the saving throw is at -2. Fear and rage counter each other.
  2. Hate: +2 to morale, saving throws, “to hit” rolls and damage. Hate and hopelessness counter each other.
  3. Hopelessness: the same effect as the symbol of hopelessness (q.v.). Countered by, and counters, hate.
  4. Rage: the recipient goes berserk: +1 “to hit”, +3 hit points of damage, and a temporary +5 hit points. It fights without a shield and without regard for its life. Countered by, and counters, fear.

Like invisibility, but the recipient can attack, with missiles, in melee or by spell casting, and stay unseen. There are sometimes telltale traces, a shimmering, so an observant opponent can attack the invisible creature, but such attacks are at -4 “to hit”, and the invisible creature makes all saving throws at +4.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the fourth level magic-user spell massmorph (q.v.).

The illusionist creates a non-living item of plant origin: soft goods, rope, wood, etc., of up to 1 cubic foot per level in volume (cf. 1e Fantasy RPG, MM, Djinni). Note the limit on the spell’s duration. The caster needs at least a tiny piece of the same kind of material: a bit of twisted hemp to make rope, a splinter of wood to make a door, and so forth.

The illusionist shapes the fears in the target’s subconscious mind into the most fearsome thing it can imagine, a horrible beast its conscious mind can see. Only the caster and the target can see it. It attacks the target as a 4 hit dice monster, and if it hits, the victim dies (of fright). It is immune to all attacks and passes through any barrier, since it exists only in the victim’s mind.

Defenses: the only defenses are to disbelieve (which can be tried only once) or to kill or knock out the illusionist. The saving throw is not standard: the target rolls 3d6 and must score its intelligence or less to disbelieve, with these modifiers:

ConditionModifier*
Complete surprise+2
Surprise+1
Subject previously attacked by this spell-1 per previous attack
Subject is an illusionist-2
Subject is wearing a helm of telepathy-3, plus the ability to turn the phantasmal killer on its creator if disbelieved

*Magic resistance and wisdom also apply. Magic resistance is checked first to see whether the spell works at all (or, for spell resistance like a dwarf’s, gnome’s, etc., -1 to -5 on the dice); then the wisdom bonus is subtracted from the roll.

If a target wearing a helm of telepathy disbelieves, it can turn the beast on the illusionist, who must then disbelieve it or be attacked, with the same possible results.

Creates semi-real phantasms of one or more monsters, all of the same kind (hobgoblins, orcs, spectres, etc.). Their total hit dice cannot exceed the illusionist’s level: a 10th level illusionist can create one monster that normally has 10 hit dice, two of 5 hit dice, etc.

Hit points: 20% of normal. Roll the normal hit dice and multiply by .20. A result less than .4 is dropped (for a monster of one hit die or less, this means it was not created); .4 or more rounds up to one hit point.

Against viewers who believe (fail their saving throw): the monsters have their normal armor class and attacks. Against viewers who save: they are armor class 10 and do only 20% of normal melee damage (bites, claws, weapons, etc.), dropping fractions below .4 as with hit points.

Example: a shadow dragonne attacks a person who knows it is only quasi-real. It attacks with 2 claws and 1 bite, hitting as a 9 die monster. All 3 hit; the normal damage rolls are 5 (d8), 8 (d8) and 11 (3d6). Multiplied by .2: .2 × 5 = 1; .2 × 8 = 1.6 = 2; .2 × 11 = 2.2 = 2; so the victim takes 5 hit points of real damage.

Like the seventh level druid spell confusion (q.v.), but every creature in the area is confused for the whole duration. Only fighters (but not paladins or rangers) and illusionists can resist, and so get a saving throw; so do monsters that do not use magic and have intelligence of 4 (semi-intelligent) or less.

Components: a small bronze disc and a small iron rod.
Like the fourth level spell shadow monsters, except that the monsters have 40% of normal hit points, do 40% of normal damage, and are armor class 8.
Like minor creation (q.v.), but the illusionist can also create mineral objects. Plant-based objects created last 12 turns per level of the caster.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the eighth level magic-user spell maze (q.v.).
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the sixth level magic-user spell project image (q.v.).

Creates the illusion of a door. The illusionist appears to step through it and vanish, but has really darted aside, and can then flee completely invisible for the spell’s duration. Creatures who open the “door” are fooled into seeing, and entering, an empty 10’ × 10’ room. Only true seeing, a gem of seeing or similar magic will reveal the illusionist.

Casts a quasi-real magic-user spell: magic missile, fireball, lightning bolt or cone of cold. Creatures in the area that fail their saving throws suffer its normal effects. Those that save take only 1 hit point of damage per level of the illusionist, whichever spell was imitated.

Conjures 1 shadow (see 1e Fantasy RPG, MM) for every three levels of the illusionist. They are under the caster’s control and attack his or her enemies on command, staying until slain or turned, or until the spell ends.

Component: a bit of smoky quartz.
Apart from the differences given in the spell’s statistics, this is the same as the sixth level cleric spell conjure animals (q.v.).

Like the fifth level spell shadow magic (q.v.), but the illusionist can also cast a quasi-real wall of fire, wall of ice or cloudkill. If a victim recognizes it as demi-shadow magic (makes its saving throw): magic missile, fireball and the rest do 2 hit points of damage per level of the caster; the walls do 1-4 hit points per level; and the cloudkill only kills creatures with fewer than 2 hit dice.

The same as the third level spell suggestion, except that it affects one creature per level of the illusionist, all within the 3” range. The suggestion must be the same for everyone who hears it. If only one creature is targeted, it saves at -2.
Creates a lasting spectral force (q.v.) that needs no concentration. It can be dispelled by dispel magic, of course.
Sets up a spectral force (q.v.) that activates on command or when a specified condition occurs (cf. magic mouth). The illusion lasts up to 1 round per level of the caster.
Related to shadow monsters and demi-shadow monsters (qq.v.), but the monsters have 60% of normal hit points and damage and are armor class 6.
Very like the fifth level cleric spell true seeing (q.v.). The illusionist sees a thing’s actual or former form, but cannot tell alignment.

The illusionist instantly changes the appearance of the surroundings and/or the party, or creates hallucinatory terrain (q.v.), well enough to fool even the cleverest creatures unless they have true seeing/sight, a gem of seeing or similar magical aid. A luxurious room can be made to look like a filthy den, and even touch matches the illusion. Hallucinatory terrain made this way does not vanish when touched.

Similar to the seventh level magic-user spell limited wish (q.v.). For the magic to take full effect, the illusionist must act out the change in reality by casting a phantasmal force, and also state it in limited words, before the spell takes effect.
The same as the seventh level cleric spell astral spell (q.v.).

system.description: Like prismatic sphere (q.v.), except that it makes a wall or curtain of shimmering colors, up to 4’ wide and 2’ high per level of the caster.

The illusionist calls on whatever power he or she wants help from, and asks the question a vision is to answer. Roll 2d6:

  • 2 to 6: the power is annoyed and, by an ultra-powerful geas or quest, makes the illusionist perform some service; no question is answered.
  • 7 to 9: the power is indifferent, and gives some minor vision, possibly unrelated to the question.
  • 10 or better: the vision is granted.

Component: the sacrifice of something valued by the caster and/or the power called upon. The more precious it is, the better the chance: a very precious item gives +1 on the dice, an extremely precious one +2, and a priceless/nonesuch item +3.
